EDITORIAL: Vote buying undermines democracy
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
16:38:14 UTC
01:38:14 KST

With campaigns for the Nov. 28 nine-in-one elections in full swing, former Financial Times Taiwan correspondent Kathrin Hille’s statement in an interview last month that “all the votes are bought” in Hualien County has sparked concern over the elections and cast a shadow over Taiwan’s democracy.
Hille, who moved to Hualien after she retired, recounted instances of neighbors mentioning who came by and put cash on the table, and said that despite Taiwan’s long-established democracy, vote buying remains common practice in the county.
Taipei Times columnist and former American Chamber of Commerce president Courtney Donovan Smith shared a similar experience: A Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) politician he was working for in Changhua County years ago openly admitted to using cash to “buy votes.”
Taiwan’s democratization after the lifting of martial law in 1987 has widely won international acclaim. Taiwan has been named by the Democracy Index a “full democracy,” and has served as a model of a robust and well-functioning democratic system.
Taiwan also stipulates higher legislative penalties for electoral bribery than most mature democracies. Under the Public Official Election and Recall Act (公職人員選罷法) and the Criminal Code, vote buyers could be fined a maximum of NT$10 million (US$314,663) and imprisoned for three to 10 years. That is higher than the US’ maximum two-year prison sentence, Japan’s three years and Germany’s five years.
However, electoral bribery cases continue in Taiwan.
Among the 5,218 people prosecuted from 2016 to last year for contravening the election and recall law, more than 91 percent were convicted of vote bribery, data from the Supreme Prosecutors’ Office and the Ministry of Justice showed.
In the 2022 local elections, the victories of more than 180 officials and councilors were invalidated after they were convicted of vote buying.
Vote buying has been a long and systemic issue in Taiwan, intertwined with political and local factions, traditional social customs, economic inequality and enormous post-election interests. Local politics has long relied on networks of kinship, factions, religious organizations, hometown associations and “voter broker.” Politicians utilize those networks to disguise vote buying as personal relationships and daily interactions, such as attending weddings and funerals, or giving gifts. Those have all blurred the lines between legality and bribery.
Hualien has long faced an electoral bribery problem, evidenced by the high number of electoral investigations and convictions. A bribery case in 2018 involving a single vote purchase of NT$10,000, as well as a major crackdown during the 2022 local elections that searched 72 locations, summoned 147 people, detained seven offenders and seized more than NT$620,000 in bribes are a few examples.
The Changhua District Prosecutors’ Office said that it has already received more than 100 reports of suspected election bribery, including at least 10 cases involving vote buying with cash.
Even Changhua County Council Speaker Hsieh Dien-lin (謝典霖) and his parents were investigated and detained last week after they were accused of vote buying — a feast in June and gifts worth more than US$1,000 — and using the council’s funds to pay for the feast.
Another issue is escalating electoral interference from China, which has been offering free trips, financial incentives and political benefits to Taiwanese, and spreading disinformation. Such interference pose a threat to Taiwan’s security and democracy, and has been a significant challenge for many Western and Asian democracies.
On the eve of the 2024 presidential and legislative elections, the Supreme Prosecutors’ Office said there were 117 cases of people contravening the Anti-Infiltration Act (反滲透法), resulting in the prosecution of 287 people. Fewer cases were reported during the 2020 elections, making it clear that China’s electoral interventions have evolved and are now sweeping in.
To eliminate electoral bribery, the government has raised the reward for whistle-blowers to NT$15 million. However, the judicial authority also needs to improve law enforcement. Current legislation does not fully disqualify convicted vote buyers from seeking re-election, so civic groups are calling for greater transparency regarding electoral cases and convicts, so that voters are aware of candidates’ criminal records and election histories.
The most important, but also the most challenging, task is to raise the public’s awareness of electoral bribery. Taiwanese must understand the value of their votes and share in the responsibility of safeguarding the election’s fairness and justice. The concept behind vote buying deterrence should transform from “passively abiding by the law” to “actively defending Taiwan’s democracy.”
Taiwan’s democracy and high-tech economy play a crucial role in global affairs and are central to the world’s embrace of a raft of next-generation technologies, including AI. It is underpinned by a security relationship with the United States that’s existed in several iterations since 1949 and the Chinese Nationalist Party’s (KMT) retreat from China. A central pillar of that security relationship is the American willingness to sell arms to Taiwan. Indeed, since 1979 it has been embedded in US law, with the Taiwan Relations Act (TRA) charging the US with helping to improve the island’s ability to deter an attack from
Academia Historica director Chen Tsui-lien (陳翠蓮), speaking at the handover ceremony for her new role on Monday, said that when she accepted the position, she knew that her peaceful life as a history professor was a thing of the past, and that from now on she would have to “wear a helmet.” A specialist in Taiwan’s post-World War II history and the 228 Incident, she has been accused of being politically divisive. Outlook for US market robust, Advantech says

16:38:09 UTC
01:38:09 KST

Industrial computer maker Advantech Co (研華) on Wednesday said that order momentum in the US should remain robust in the second half of this year, supported by continued growth in the healthcare, semiconductor equipment and robotics businesses.
The company’s US book-to-bill ratio currently stands at 2.15 and is expected to stay at about 2 throughout this year, well above the company’s overall ratio of 1.4, Advantech North America general manager Ween Niu (牛文中) told a news conference in Taipei.
Design wins in the US market in the first half of the year already surpassed the US$420 million it gained for the whole of last year, Niu said.
Photo: Fang Wei-chieh, Taipei Times
A design win refers to a customer’s decision to adopt a supplier’s solution for a new product development project, suggesting orders from the customer and revenue contribution in the future.
US design wins in the second half are expected to be flat or higher compared with the first half, with the full-year total at least double that of last year, Niu said.
They are expected to start contributing to revenue in 2028, he added.
The US market generated US$430 million in revenue in the first half, accounting for 29 percent of the company’s total, he said.
US revenue in the second half is expected to rise at least 50 percent from the first half, and lift full-year sales to US$1 billion, he said.
Regarding the company’s healthcare business, Niu said Advantech works with 28 of the 30 largest US medical equipment makers, providing customers with hardware and system integration related to surgical robots, medical imaging and surgical navigation.
Advantech aims to expand from individual projects and standardized products into multiple equipment platforms, he said.
Its semiconductor equipment business is also growing fast in North America, with the company working with the three largest US semiconductor equipment makers, Niu said.
Revenue from this segment grew 75 percent year-on-year in the first half and is expected to increase about 120 percent next year, he said.
In robotics, Advantech is in talks on more than 20 projects in the US, with more than five entering the contract-signing stage, he said.
As humanoid robotics development is still in the early phase, the company aims to expand its customer base first, he said.
To ease capacity constraints amid robust US demand, Advantech offers overtime incentives and is accelerating the transfer of about 32 projects from its manufacturing site in northern California to a new southern California site in Tustin, Niu said, adding that US capacity is expected to match demand in the second half of next year.
The Tustin site, which began small-volume production in May and is scheduled to enter full operations next month, is expected to contribute more than US$80 million in revenue this year and about US$300 million next year, Niu said.
The site is expected to account for about 40 percent of Advantech’s total US production capacity after 2028, he said.

Alexander Lukashenko pardons another 15 people, including 13 convicted of what Belarus calls ‘extremist’ crimes
Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko has signed a decree pardoning 15 people, according to BelTA.
Thirteen of them were convicted of what BelTA called “extremist offenses.” Ten of those pardoned are women. Their names were not disclosed.
BelTA noted that all 15 petitioned for pardons, admitted guilt, expressed remorse for what they had done, and “promised to lead law-abiding lives.”
Since 2025, Lukashenko has periodically released people convicted on political charges as part of an agreement with the U.S. to lift sanctions in exchange for their release. Those pardoned have included opposition leaders Viktor Babariko and Maria Kolesnikova, among many others. Hundreds of political prisoners remain in Belarus, however. The human rights group Viasna puts the number at more than 800.

Armiia+ app connected to NBU BankID system for user authentication
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
19:34:34 EEST
01:34:34 KST

The Armiia+ mobile app for military personnel has been directly connected to the National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) BankID system for user authentication, the regulator's press service reported.
"One of the state's objectives is to ensure citizens have convenient, reliable, and secure access to digital services. Connecting the Armiia+ mobile app directly to the NBU BankID system is an important step in this direction, as it will make authentication even easier for military personnel," said Olha Vasylyeva, Deputy Director of the NBU's Payment Systems and Innovative Development Department.
Previously, authentication in Armia+ was carried out exclusively via the integrated electronic identification system of the Diia state portal.
The direct connection of the Armiia+ app to NBU BankID—implemented through cooperation between the National Bank and the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine—will reduce the time required for military personnel to authenticate.
According to the National Bank, as of July 1, 2026, the BankID system comprised 37 identification providers and 117 service providers (102 commercial and 15 non-commercial).

Trump invites Putin to Miami G20: Why that matters
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
16:32:56 UTC
01:32:56 KST

Trump invites Putin to Miami G20: Why that matters
US Secretary of State Rubio said the summit would be an ‘opportunity’ for Putin to engage with other world leaders.
United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio has announced that Washington has invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to December’s G20 meeting in Miami amid efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war.
Following a meeting with Russian Foreign Secretary Sergey Lavrov on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Wednesday, Rubio said the US remained open to speaking with Moscow about Ukraine.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3The view from Russia: ‘No party can be antiwar’ in parliamentary election
- list 2 of 3Trump-Xi summit: Here’s what’s on the agenda, and why it matters
- list 3 of 3China vs US: Who is winning the AI race, in four charts
“We’ve just invited President Putin to the G20. We think it’s an opportunity for him to engage not just with the president but with other world leaders. We hope that’s an invitation he’ll accept,” Rubio said.
Trump and Putin last met, face to face, in Anchorage, Alaska, in August 2025, but failed to reach any agreement over Ukraine. Putin has not visited the contiguous United States since he invaded Ukraine in 2022.
Here’s what we know.
What is the G20?
The G20, or Group of 20, is a forum bringing together the world’s major and emerging economies. A summit is held annually – this year in Miami, Florida, in the US.
Those countries or groups of countries are:
- Argentina
- Australia
- Brazil
- Canada
- China
- France
- Germany
- India
- Indonesia
- Italy
- Japan
- Mexico
- Russia
- Saudi Arabia
- South Africa
- South Korea
- Turkiye
- United Kingdom
- United States
- African Union
- European Union
While many G20 countries, such as Germany, France, and the UK, are allied with Ukraine, others have closer ties with Russia – including China and India.
If he accepts the invitation, it would be Putin’s first in-person attendance at a G20 summit since 2019.
In 2021, the Russian leader attended the G20 summit virtually and spoke by video feed, but in 2023, when the summit was held in India, Putin sent Lavrov in his place.
What has Russia said?
On Thursday, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said no decision had been taken about Putin’s attendance at the December summit.
When asked what the two leaders might discuss, Peskov told reporters, “It is premature to speak about this right now.”
“No decision has been made yet. We certainly appreciate this kind invitation, we value it, and it will be reviewed and coordinated, after which an appropriate decision will be reached.”
The spokesperson reiterated that Russia is seeking a peace settlement, not a temporary ceasefire.
How are US-Russian relations?
While the US maintains contact with Moscow for dialogue over the war in Ukraine, relations between the countries are strained.
Last week, Trump signed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026 into law, which grants the president sweeping powers to sanction buyers of Russian energy, in a bid to pressure Moscow to end the war.
The legislation, named after the late hawkish Republican lawmaker, also sanctions President Vladimir Putin, senior officials and oligarchs, along with Russian banks and financial institutions.
However, this week, Trump appeared to contradict this approach when he called on Ukraine to agree to an “energy truce” with Russia whereby both sides stop launching strikes on each other’s energy facilities and infrastructure. In comments to reporters at the UN headquarters, Zelenskyy said Kyiv would halt strikes on Russian energy facilities if Moscow stopped targeting Ukraine’s energy systems, as well.
Trump has blamed the Ukraine-Russia war for the current record rise in diesel prices in the United States, which has become a major issue as the country approaches midterm elections in November, adding that Ukraine’s strikes on Russian diesel facilities were “hurting the world”.
But observers said Trump is placing pressure on the wrong actor in the war.
“It is Russia’s – not Ukraine’s – responsibility to end the attacks,” Marnie Howlett, an associate professor of international relations in Eastern Europe and Eurasia at the University of Oxford, told Al Jazeera. “The Russian Federation has repeatedly broken ceasefire agreements, so the war will continue until it agrees to recognise Ukraine’s territorial sovereignty.”
“The ongoing sales of Russian fossil fuels continue to finance Russia’s war against Ukraine,” Amanda Paul, senior policy analyst at the European Policy Centre (EPC), said.
“Rather than putting the emphasis on the impact of Ukrainian strikes on fuel prices, Trump should be putting greater pressure on Russia to end its attacks and bring the war to an end,” she said. “Trump himself is responsible for stoking high energy prices, due to the repercussions of the US-Israel war on Iran and the subsequent blocking of the Strait of Hormuz.”
Was the G20 invitation for Putin expected this year?
Last month, US media reported that the head of the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), John Ratcliffe, travelled to Moscow for unannounced talks.
According to CBS News, news of his trip came only after an Air Force Boeing C-17 Globemaster III transport plane was spotted flying into a Moscow airport.
While the CIA did not comment on his trip, Peskov told reporters in Moscow that Ratcliffe had spoken to Russian intelligence officials, but did not meet Putin. Then, a senior Ukrainian official told CBS that Washington had told Ukraine that a US delegation would be travelling to Moscow and asked Kyiv to pause its attacks until the delegation left.
On Wednesday, citing two sources familiar with the matter, the Reuters news agency reported that Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev would go to the US to meet special envoy Steve Witkoff and Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner.
According to one source, the visit aims to keep Russia-US dialogue and peacekeeping efforts going. Economic cooperation, energy issues and a peace settlement in Ukraine will also be on the agenda.
Will Putin’s visit trigger the International Criminal Court (ICC) warrant for his arrest?
No.
In March 2023, the ICC issued a warrant for Putin’s arrest for the alleged war crime of unlawfully deporting Ukrainian children to Russia.
Under the Rome Statute, the international treaty that established the ICC, signatories are obliged to carry out the warrant if a person with a warrant for their arrest enters their territory.
However, the US is not a signatory to the Rome Statute and will therefore not abide by it. Furthermore, the Trump administration is reported to be preparing sanctions against the ICC, which has also issued a warrant for the arrest of Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on suspicion of war crimes in Gaza. The US has previously also placed sanctions on ICC officials.
The new US sanctions would prohibit most transactions with the ICC after a grace period of six to seven months, The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday. If imposed, the measures would bar US citizens and companies from providing the ICC with money, goods or services without a licence from the US Department of the Treasury. Banks and other companies often take an especially cautious approach to US sanctions because they rely on access to the US financial system.
On Thursday, Trump urged all countries that are members of the ICC to quit and said it was “out of control”.
“The United States is equally opposed to the out-of-control institution known as the International Criminal Court,” he told the United Nations General Assembly. “I call on all nations that are members of the ICC to officially resign from this rogue institution immediately.”
How have other countries responded to Putin’s invitation to the G20?
Kaja Kallas, the European Union’s high representative for foreign affairs, criticised the invitation and said she would raise it with other members of the G20.
“We need to discuss this together with colleagues, but it’s clearly, I think, the wrong path to normalise people who are starting wars, who are going against the UN charter, who are killing and giving orders to kill civilians, to ignore the international humanitarian law, to cause as much damage and suffering to people that they can,” she added.
“By normalising this, believe me, we will have more of it around the world.”
On Thursday, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, a Ukraine ally, said inviting Putin to the Miami summit could encourage Moscow to continue its attacks on Ukraine.
“If inviting Putin to the G20 could bring us closer to a just peace, I would be absolutely in favour of it,” Tusk told a news conference.
“However – and this is both my concern and what my experience tells me – at this stage, Russia might well view it as an encouragement to continue its aggressive policies. That is what I fear.”

UK PM informs Zelenskyy he will maintain sanctions against Russian oligarchs – Bloomberg
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has informed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that he disagrees with the European Union's decision to lift sanctions against Russian billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman.
Source: European Pravda, citing sources familiar with the situation quoted by Bloomberg
Details: According to these sources, Burnham made these comments during a meeting with Zelenskyy on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York this week.
The UK prime minister also informed Zelenskyy that the United Kingdom will not lift sanctions against Usmanov and Fridman, sources noted. He stated that Ukraine's allies should continue to maintain their sanctions to exert pressure on Russia to end the war.
A Downing Street statement on Burnham's meeting with Zelenskyy made no mention of the EU decision but noted that the prime minister spoke about the "need to keep increasing pressure on Russia through sanctions to ensure he came to the table".
This criticism points to a rare rift between the UK and the EU over sanctions against Russia, which had largely been aligned since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Both Fridman and Usmanov had interests in the UK. Usmanov is best known internationally for his investments in London's Arsenal football club, which he exited in 2018. Fridman moved to London in 2013 but left the country after sanctions were imposed against him.
Background: The Council of the EU adopted a final decision on 22 September to extend sanctions against individuals and entities responsible for undermining or threatening Ukraine's territorial integrity, sovereignty and independence for a further 36 months. However, it has removed two Russian oligarchs from the list.

Police arrested a high school principal in the Negev on suspicion of slapping and biting a student during a brawl. Following questioning, the principal was released to five days of house arrest under restrictive conditions. Police at the Ayarot station are continuing to investigate the circumstances of the incident. The case was first reported by Reshet News.
The principal was the one who called police more than a week ago to report the brawl. The investigation found that his son and nephew were also suspected of being involved in the altercation. Investigators took statements from those involved, with one student saying the principal shoved him, bit him and slapped him. The principal was questioned under caution and later released to his home.
The principal gave his account in a letter sent to fellow school principals. He said: "Several days ago, a 12th-grade student called my son at night and began making serious threats against him and me, while also hurling curses and insults at us. We did not understand the reason for his behavior. That same night, I contacted the student's parents but did not receive an adequate response. Immediately afterward, I reported the threats to Israel Police and requested a police presence at the school the following morning."
The principal continued: "The next day, despite an agreement with the parents that the student would be barred from school, he arrived at the school, ambushed my son and brutally attacked him solely because he is the principal's son. He later tried to reach my office to physically harm me, and only the quick thinking of teachers at the school prevented him from doing so. Police arrived only after the attack, and I filed a formal complaint. At the end of the school day, I was asked to come to the Ayarot police station to give a statement."
'Fingerprinting in a humiliating and degrading manner'
The principal, who is suspected of assaulting the student, said he was surprised to discover at the police station that he was being detained and questioned under caution.
"My cellphone was taken from me, and I was placed in a detention cell with other detainees," he said. "I underwent identification procedures, was photographed and had my fingerprints taken in a humiliating and degrading manner. Only during questioning did I learn that the student who attacked us had filed a baseless assault complaint against me. The investigator treated me dismissively and did not listen to my account."
The principal added: "At the end of the questioning, I was released on bail to five days of full house arrest, while the violent student remains free. The following day, when my two sons went to the police station to file a complaint, they were arrested and also placed under house arrest. After looking into the matter, I learned that someone had posted content criticizing the student on TikTok. The student demanded that I, as principal, remove the post. When that did not happen, he decided to take revenge on my children and me.
"I am now sitting at home with very difficult feelings. In dealing with the police, the Education Ministry, the Teachers' Association and the local council, I feel completely alone. We acted properly, followed the law and made all the required reports, but in the end, they turned us — the victims — into criminals. It is an upside-down world devoid of justice.
"After a quarter-century devoted to education, working day and night for the sake of our students, I have reached the painful conclusion that in today's crazy reality — with no institutional support and violence running rampant — it simply does not pay to be a school principal."

Russian budget deficit to be 2.2% of GDP next year — Finance Minister
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
16:28:53 UTC
01:28:53 KST

MOSCOW, September 24. /TASS/. The Russian federal budget deficit in 2027 will amount to 2.2% of GDP, Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said at a Russian government meeting.
"Expenditures will total 48.8 trillion rubles ($574.1 bln), while revenues will stand at 43.3 trillion rubles ($509.4 bln). The budget deficit is set at around 2% of GDP for the next three years. In 2027, the budget deficit will amount to 2.2% of GDP. In conclusion, I would like to note that the prepared budget is balanced, which is important for maintaining macroeconomic stability, lowering inflation and interest rates, and driving the growth of real disposable public income, which will reach 1.4% next year," the minister said.
A smooth transition to the fiscal rule will be achieved by 2029, Siluanov noted. During the transition period in 2027-2028, the maximum expenditure limit will exceed the structural level by 1.5 trillion and 0.5 trillion rubles ($17.6 bln and $5.8 bln), respectively, the minister added.
"The budget is resilient to various scenarios. Starting next year, the base price of Urals crude oil is factored in at $50 per barrel for a three-year period. This means all obligations will be funded at this oil price level. If market conditions are more favorable, we will replenish the National Wealth Fund," Siluanov said.

Russia’s economy minister outlines key drivers of growth

MOSCOW, September 24. /TASS/. Economic Development Minister Maxim Reshetnikov, presenting Russia’s socioeconomic development forecast at a government meeting, described consumer demand as a key driver of economic growth and said it was expected to increase significantly, by 4.1%, in 2026. The minister also pointed to rising household incomes.
"Consumer demand remains a key driver of economic growth. This year, we expect it to increase significantly, by 4.1%. Consumer activity is supported by rising household incomes. U.K. prime minister teases possible return of booze to soccer matches
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
16:27:19 UTC
01:27:19 KST

Could U.K. soccer fans get their beers back? Prime Minister Andy Burnham teases possible end of 40-year ban
London — British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called the ban on alcohol in the stands at high-level men's soccer matches in the U.K. "discrimination," teasing fellow fans with a possible reversal of a more than 40-year-old ban.
"I don't think it's fair for football fans to be singled out," Burnham told reporters in New York on Wednesday, where he is attending the United Nations General Assembly.
He hinted at a trial to reintroduce alcohol consumption in stadium seating.
The U.K. government, under then-Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher, banned alcohol in the bleachers at men's soccer games in England and Wales in 1985.
Home Secretary Leon Brittan said at the time that booze was a "major contributory factor in violent and disorderly behavior" in soccer stadiums.
Since then, fans attending men's soccer games in the top five divisions have not been allowed to drink alcohol in view of the pitch. People can still buy and drink alcohol in the concourse before games and during halftime, but they cannot carry it back to their seats.
No other sports are subject to such a ban in the U.K.
At some older, less well-equipped soccer grounds, lines for pints of beer can get so long during halftime that fans will leave their seats before the referee blows the whistle.
In a statement, the Football Supporters' Association said Thursday that it has "always argued that it's unfair to criminalize football fans for having a pint while watching the match," and it argued that many clubs are in favor of a reintroduction of alcohol, adding: "We welcome the prime minister's comments and totally agree that the legislation is outdated."
After a successful pilot run in the Women's Super League, the highest level of English women's soccer, fans of the women's game have been allowed to drink in the stands since the beginning of the current season.
Burnham, who's a season ticket holder at Premier League club Everton, criticized the restriction shortly before becoming prime minister.
Asked Wednesday if he still held the same view, he said: "I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different … And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination. There are different ways it could be done. It could happen on a trial basis."
"I'm not going to back away from what's been a long-held view of mine," he said. "I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently."
The ban was imposed with reason, however.
Soccer hooliganism in 1970s and 1980s England — sometimes referred to as the "English Disease" — involved fans in rival gangs linked to soccer clubs fighting each other and vandalizing areas in and around stadiums.
Several high-profile deaths linked to hooliganism, including that of a 14-year-old boy who died when fans were pushed into a wall by police after violence between Birmingham City and Leeds United fans, led to the alcohol ban.
Police have long supported the legislation.
"Other sports simply don't see the violence and criminal behavior from their supporters that football does, albeit a minority, with alcohol often playing a significant part in violent and disorderly behavior," a spokesperson for the U.K.'s Football Policing Unit said, according to CBS News' U.K. partner network the BBC.
"It would be irresponsible to fuel this by allowing greater alcohol consumption during games," they said, adding that it would be "incredibly rash to make fundamental changes without a full examination of the evidence and meaningful consultation with police practitioners who have the expertise in this area."
A fan-led review of U.K. laws around soccer in 2021 called for the legislation to be reviewed, however.
In Scotland, which also has a history of soccer-related violence, alcohol has been banned from soccer stadiums since 1981, but recent trials have seen it reintroduced, and fans can now buy booze at games at Hampden Park, the country's national soccer stadium.

Finland had planned to deport a Russian mother and son who helped Ukrainian refugees. Instead, it’s granting them asylum.
Finland has granted asylum to Russian nationals Olga and Nikita Belov, former St. Petersburg municipal councilor Svetlana Utkina told TV Rain. Finnish authorities had planned to deport the mother and son to Russia this spring.
The Belovs left Russia after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine began. Nikita Belov said he decided to leave after refusing to take part in an “unnamed secret project” at the I.P. Bardin Central Research Institute of Ferrous Metallurgy. He said the institute’s management assured him the project was unrelated to the war, but he later learned otherwise.
In Finland, the Belovs helped Ukrainian refugees through the volunteer organization FinEst Volunteers. In spring 2026, they were summoned to a police station and told they would be deported. In August, a court ordered a review of their case. The Belovs’ lawyer said the family had provided “a great deal of new evidence” that they could face persecution in Russia.

Xi says ready to work with Trump to steer China-U.S. ties on steady course
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-25
00:26:39 CST
01:26:39 KST

WASHINGTON, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Thursday that he is ready to work with U.S. President Donald Trump to steer the giant ship of China-U.S. relationship on a steady course toward the future.
Addressing an arrival ceremony at the White House, Xi said that he is visiting the United States at Trump's invitation to carry on their friendship, expand cooperation and promote the well-being of the two peoples.
China and the United States should strengthen communication, cooperate with sincerity and coexist in peace, he noted.
Xi said he and Trump encourage government departments, such as those in charge of foreign affairs, economic matters, financial cooperation, law enforcement and people-to-people exchanges, to catch up on strengthening contact.
China-U.S. cooperation may not solve every problem in the world, but without it, it would be hard to solve many of the world's problems, Xi said.
China keeps its door wide open, welcomes American companies wanting to invest and do business in China, Xi said. "We hope Chinese companies are treated fairly here in the United States. Working together, we can lengthen the list of cooperation and shorten the list of issues."
Both China and the United States are leading nations in artificial intelligence (AI), Xi said, noting that the two countries have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control and serves the well-being of the people.
On counternarcotics and law enforcement, the Chinese side is willing to strengthen cooperation with the United States, Xi said. "Our two sides may also increase direct flights to facilitate two-way travel and trade."
China and the United States do not need to avoid mentioning competition, but the competition should be a healthy one and should be kept within bounds, he said, adding that it should be a race of catching up with one another, not a wrestle in which one either wins or loses.
China and the United States must hold the line of no conflict and no confrontation, Xi said. "We can certainly find the right path for our two great countries to get along on this planet we both call home."
Chinese and U.S. militaries should maintain regular dialogue and improve mechanisms for crisis communication and prevention, Xi said, adding that the Thucydides Trap can be overcome.
Xi announced an invitation for 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchanges and study in the coming five years. He also declared that in a few days, a pair of pandas will come to their new home in Zoo Atlanta and meet with the American people. ■

Rwandan coffee generated 148.6 mln USD in 2025/2026 financial year: official
China

00:26:28 CST
01:26:28 KST

KIGALI, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- Rwanda's coffee generated a record 148.6 million U.S. dollars in the 2025/2026 financial year, a senior official said Thursday.
Rwandan Minister of Gender and Family Promotion Consolee Uwimana made the remarks while opening a global coffee conference in Kigali, the Rwandan capital city.
The conference, due to close on Friday, brought together women coffee producers, buyers, roasters, policymakers, researchers, investors, and industry partners to connect, exchange ideas, and build meaningful partnerships and solutions.
The global coffee conference was convened by Sustainable Growers Rwanda, an organization focused on unlocking the potential of women smallholder coffee farmers in East Africa.
The minister said the revenues generated from coffee demonstrate the strength and potential of the country's coffee sector in economic development.
"But this growth must be reflected in the pockets of our women. Women may produce coffee and create its value, yet remain excluded from the decisions, capital and market that determine who will receive it. Participation is not ownership, and producing value is not the same as having a stake in it," Uwimana said.
More than 250 participants from Africa, Europe, Asia, North America and Latin America convened to learn from the farmers behind the coffee before discussing the future of the industry, according to organizers.
It provided a platform to explore new opportunities, share knowledge, and advance a more inclusive, resilient, and sustainable future for coffee. ■

CHONGQING, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- China beat the Maldives 3-0 in the opening match of the CFA Team China International Football Competitions Chongqing on Thursday, with Wang Ziming scoring a second-half hat-trick.

Wang completed his hat-trick on the hour mark, applying a deft finish near the six-yard box after Wang Gengrui's cross from the flank.
Many players made their senior national team debut, while high school student Zhao Songyuan became the youngest player ever to represent China's men's national team.
Head coach Shao Jiayi is expected to use the four matches to experiment his squad and assess new players ahead of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia.
At the post-match press conference, Shao said that the team had carried out its pre-match plans well in terms of achieving its objectives, adding that China had not played a competitive match for nearly three weeks, and that it would take time for the players to get back in sharp form.

Macklemore announces 'Free Palestine Tour' after Sheeran split
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
16:26:16 UTC
01:26:16 KST

Breadcrumb
Macklemore hits back with 'Free Palestine Tour' after Sheeran split
US rapper Macklemore, who was dropped from British pop star Ed Sheeran's tour after saying 'Free Palestine', comments, announced Thursday he will instead perform on his own "Free Palestine Tour."
Macklemore, who was opening for Sheeran's "Loop Tour," shouted "Free Palestine!" and told Palestinians they were "not forgotten" during two concerts earlier this month in New Jersey.
The "Thrift Shop" star was quickly booted from the US tour -- a decision that Sheeran said was made by tour promoters, not him -- provoking outrage among musicians and pro-Palestinian activists.
"What happened to me is bigger than one artist or one stage," Macklemore, 43, said in an Instagram post.
"When the billionaire class can decide which voices are allowed on stage and which ones are too dangerous to hear, everyone should be paying attention," he added.
Macklemore announced three shows in London, Paris and Dublin for late October, with US dates also planned, and said all proceeds will benefit pro-Palestinian organisations.
"It's 2026. Being apolitical during a genocide doesn't work anymore," he said.
"People are asking artists to show up, educate themselves and be in community. To use the stage for more than entertainment. To push back when the call for a Free Palestine is met with attempts to silence it."
Macklemore's removal has opened a can of worms for the Grammy-winning Sheeran, who says he steers clear of making "political" statements, despite performing at a benefit concert in support of Ukraine after Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.
Last weekend at a show in Philadelphia, he opened the performance with a statement on the controversy, calling the 7 October attacks on Israel "horrific" and describing the situation in Gaza as "catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate". Sheeran also described the situation in Palestine as the "most complex political issue on the planet", drawing further criticism from pro-Palestine activists.
"I've had to take and make difficult decisions, and I am making mistakes, and I'm so, so sorry," an emotional Sheeran told his audience, who responded with cheers. At the end of the show, Sheeran tearfully said "the one thing I would like to apologise for is the first bit of the show where it wasn't about music and I had to talk."
Four other supporting artists, including American singer Finneas, have also pulled out of Sheeran's tour in solidarity with Macklemore and Palestine.

====================================================================================================

Copper boom to boost Russia's export revenue, to attract investments — expert
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
16:26:04 UTC
01:26:04 KST

MOSCOW, September 24. /TASS/. Rapid growth in global demand for copper opens up opportunities for Russia to increase its export revenue and attract investment into domestic mining and metallurgical companies and projects, Pavel Gamov, an expert on the mining and metals industry at the Stolypin Institute for Growth Economics, told TASS.
Earlier, Kirill Dmitriev, Russian Presidential Special Representative for Investment and Economic Cooperation with Foreign Countries and head of the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF), called copper the "new gold."
"For Russia, the copper boom represents a direct boost to export revenues and the investment appeal of Nornickel, UMMC, RMK, Udokan, and the Baimsky GOK," Gamov said.
According to him, the growing need for the metal is linked to developments in the energy sector and artificial intelligence technologies, while options to expand production are limited.
"Demand is being driven by electrification, power grids, renewable energy sources, and AI data centers, whereas supply is constrained: it takes 12-15 years to build a new mine, and mature deposits are becoming depleted," the expert explained.
The expert noted that Russia supplies about 4% of the world's refined copper - roughly 1 million tons annually, with exports accounting for approximately 600,000 tons.
"By 2040, global demand for copper could rise by approximately 50%, while the deficit could reach 10 million tons per year," Gamov noted.
At the same time, the expert pointed out that high prices do not eliminate the impact of sanctions, increased logistics costs, difficulties with banking settlements, and discounts for Russian suppliers. "Rising metal prices also drive up the production costs of cables, electrical equipment, and the construction and modernization of grids within Russia," Gamov concluded.

====================================================================================================

Mysterious death of Catalan architect Josep Juanpere: partner arrested, key witness in coma
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
16:26:03 UTC
01:26:03 KST

Nine months after architect Josep Juanpere died in Baqueira, police have arrested his partner; the nephew who found the body is in a coma and the first autopsy showed no signs of violence.
A new and mysterious case has shaken Catalan society. Nine months after the death of renowned architect Josep Juanpere at his home in Baqueira, what initially appeared to be a death from natural causes has taken an unexpected turn: the Catalan police have arrested his partner over her alleged involvement in his death.
Juanpere, 72, had gone to Vielha hospital just two days before he died, after feeling unwell. The first autopsy found no signs of violence, but doubts about the circumstances of his death led to an investigation which, months later, has resulted this week in the arrest of the woman who was with him during his final hours.
The architect died on 26 December 2025 at his second home in Baqueira, in the Val d'Aran (Lleida), where he was spending the Christmas holidays with his partner. Two days earlier, on Christmas Eve, he had gone to Vielha hospital after feeling unwell and remained there for several hours under observation.
Initially, everything pointed to a natural death. The first forensic examination found no signs of violence and attributed the death to a coronary problem. However, the circumstances of his death ended up under investigation by the court in Vielha, which is keeping proceedings under seal.
The case has taken a turn this week with the arrest in Madrid of Juanpere's partner, a woman of around 63, over her alleged connection to the architect's death. According to 'El Mundo', she comes from a family that made its fortune in the property and hotel sectors and maintains close links with prominent social and business circles.
Investigators have also carried out searches and other procedural steps while the detainee awaits her appearance before the court handling the case.
Another development has now added to concern around the investigation: Juanpere's nephew, regarded as a key witness because he was the one who found the architect's body, is in a coma, according to 'El Confidencial'. He has been in a private clinic for weeks with a lung condition, the newspaper reports.
From Vielha hospital to his death in Baqueira
The last 48 hours of Juanpere's life are one of the key elements in the case. The architect began to feel unwell on 24 December and went to Vielha hospital, where he was treated and kept under observation for several hours, according to local media. He later returned to the house in Baqueira where he was spending Christmas.
Two days later, on 26 December, he was found dead in the property. According to reports on the investigation, members of Juanpere's family had tried to contact him without success. Eventually, one of his nephews went to the house and spent nearly an hour at the door, ringing without getting an answer, until the architect's partner let him in. Once inside, he found Juanpere dead and the woman apparently in a state of shock, according to 'El Periódico'.
At that point, nothing obviously pointed to a violent death, although one detail raised questions: Juanpere's partner had not previously called the emergency services. The body showed no external signs of violence and the first forensic conclusions pointed to death from natural causes.
However, the case did not close. The circumstances surrounding the death led investigators to continue their inquiries, and the court in Vielha eventually opened an investigation that has been conducted for months with great discretion.
The nephew who found Juanpere, in a coma
Josep Juanpere's nephew, a key figure in reconstructing the circumstances in which the architect was found, is currently in a coma, according to 'El Confidencial'.
He was the one who went to the house in Baqueira on 26 December after the family had been unable to contact Juanpere. His account is particularly important to investigators because he was one of the first people to enter the house after Juanpere's death and was able to see directly the state of the property and of those present.
A first autopsy that found no signs of violence
One of the main unanswered questions lies precisely in the initial forensic findings. The first autopsy found no indication of violence and pointed to a coronary problem as the cause of death. Those conclusions explain why Juanpere's death was initially treated as a natural one.
Subsequent investigations, however, led to the widening of inquiries into what happened during his final hours. Nine months on, investigators believe that there is sufficient evidence to investigate a possible criminal death and to arrest the person who was with the architect during those days.
The secrecy surrounding the proceedings makes it impossible for now to know exactly what evidence has prompted this change of course, or what investigators' precise theory is on how the death may have occurred. Nor have all the results of the later forensic tests, or the element that proved decisive in turning a death initially deemed natural into one now being investigated as a possible homicide, been made public.
Juanpere's partner arrested
The woman who was with Juanpere that Christmas is now at the centre of the investigation. The Catalan police have arrested her in Madrid over her alleged involvement in the architect's death, after roughly nine months of inquiries.
Investigators have tried to reconstruct what happened between Juanpere's visit to hospital on 24 December and his death two days later, a period considered crucial to clarifying the case.
The detainee must appear before the judicial authorities, and it will be for the judge to determine her legal status and decide on any precautionary measures. Her arrest does not amount to a declaration of guilt and, as the proceedings move forward, she continues to be protected by the presumption of innocence.
Searches and an investigation under seal
The arrest has been accompanied by new police actions linked to the investigation. The case remains under seal, so very few details have emerged about the evidence gathered over these nine months or about the elements investigators consider important for clarifying the death.
This lack of information helps explain why some of the main questions in the case remain open: what happened after Juanpere returned from hospital, what took place during his final hours and what investigators have discovered to move from an apparently natural death to looking into a possible criminal killing.
The answers will now depend on the progress of the judicial investigation and on the outcome of the measures carried out.
Who was Josep Juanpere?
Josep Juanpere i Miret was co-founder of GCA Architects, one of Spain's architecture and interior design firms with the strongest presence in corporate, hotel and residential projects. Juanpere set up the practice in Barcelona in 1986 together with Antonio Puig. Over the years, GCA took part in numerous projects for major national and international companies and brands.
Juanpere also had a close friendship with Isak Andic, founder of Mango, whose death likewise ended up under judicial investigation. Andic died in December 2024 after falling down a ravine during an excursion in Montserrat. The case, initially closed and later reopened, ultimately placed his son Jonathan Andic under investigation; he was arrested in May 2026 over his alleged involvement in his father's death.
The relationship between Juanpere and Andic went beyond the personal sphere. GCA Architects worked for Mango on various projects, and Juanpere was responsible for the interior design of the 'Nirvana Formentera', Andic's sailing yacht. After the businessman's death, Juanpere penned an emotional farewell in which he described him as a "great friend".

Full text: Xi's remarks at arrival ceremony at the White House
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-25
00:26:01 CST
01:26:01 KST

WASHINGTON, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday gave remarks at the arrival ceremony at the White House in Washington, D.C., the United States.
The following is the full text of the remarks:
Honorable President Donald J. Trump and Mrs. Melania Trump,
Ladies and Gentlemen,
Dear Friends,
I'm very glad to pay a state visit to your beautiful country, the United States of America. Thank you, President Trump and Mrs. Trump, for the warm hospitality you have extended to me and my wife. On behalf of the 1.4 billion and more Chinese people, I wish to begin by extending sincere greetings to the American people and warm congratulations on the 250th anniversary of the U.S. independence.
Both China and the United States are great countries, and both the Chinese and American peoples are great peoples. I am visiting the United States at President Trump's invitation to carry on our friendship, expand cooperation, and promote the well-being of both our peoples.
Facing the changes in our world, in our times, and of historical significance today, China and the United States, as two major countries, shoulder a historic responsibility of advancing human development and progress.
Mr. President, during your visit to China this year, we agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and this is widely welcomed by the people of our two countries and the international community. I am ready to work with you to steer the giant ship of China-U.S. relationship on a steady course toward the future.
-- We should strengthen communication. China and the United States are different in national conditions, but through candid, in-depth and continued dialogue, our two countries can understand each other better, seek common ground while shelving differences, and build up mutual trust. President Trump and I have respect for each other. We have built personal rapport and stayed in touch. We encourage our government departments, such as those in charge of foreign affairs, economic matters, financial cooperation, law enforcement and people-to-people exchanges, to catch up on strengthening contact, and we support our legislative bodies in increasing exchanges.
-- We should cooperate with sincerity. The interests of China and the United States are deeply intertwined, and there is plenty of room for us to work together. China-U.S. cooperation may not solve every problem in the world. But, without our cooperation, it would be hard to solve many of the world's problems. China keeps its door wide open, welcomes American companies wanting to invest and do business there. We hope Chinese companies are treated fairly here in the United States. Working together, we can lengthen the list of cooperation, and shorten the list of issues. Both China and the United States are leading nations in artificial intelligence. We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good, and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control and serves the well-being of the people. On counternarcotics and law enforcement, the Chinese side is willing to strengthen cooperation with the United States. Our two sides may also increase direct flights to facilitate two-way travel and trade.
-- We should coexist in peace. As I have said many times, China and the United States, as two major countries, stand to gain from cooperation and will both lose in confrontation. We do not need to avoid mentioning competition, but our competition should be a healthy one and should be kept within bounds. It should be a race of catching up with one another, not a wrestle in which one either wins or loses. China and the United States must hold the line of no conflict and no confrontation between us, and we can certainly find the right path for our two great countries to get along on this planet we both call home. Our two militaries should maintain regular dialogue, and improve mechanisms for crisis communication and prevention. The Thucydides Trap can be overcome.
Ladies and Gentlemen,
Dear Friends,
During the Second World War, Chinese and Americans fought shoulder to shoulder against fascist aggression. Chinese people have never forgotten that part of history, nor have the American people. The hope of the China-U.S. relationship lies in our people, and its future lies with the young. I am glad to announce an invitation for 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchanges and study in the coming five years.
The giant panda has been an envoy of friendship between the Chinese and Americans. Here, I have a piece of good news. In a few days, two pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, will come to their new home in Zoo Atlanta and meet with the American people.
Ladies and Gentlemen,
Dear Friends,
Achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand in hand. Let us meet the people's expectation and show our historical initiative. Let us keep advancing the cause of friendship between our two peoples and work together to build a better world!
Thank you. ■

Egypt seeks closer business cooperation with China: minister

Israel's Palestinian parties hit back at 'racist' election ban
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
16:22:31 UTC
01:22:31 KST

Breadcrumb
'Hypocrisy': Israel's Palestinian parties hit back over election ban
The Joint List of Israel's Palestinian parties has condemned its ban from the upcoming Knesset elections in October, telling The New Arab that the decisions are "based on racism" and reflect the "hypocrisy of those who claim to support democracy".
The Joint List, made up of Hadash, Ta'al and Balad, is one of two major Arab-Israeli political blocs representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, the other being the United Arab List (Ra'am), which was also barred from the election.
Both lists were barred by Israel's Central Elections Committee (CEC) on Wednesday, which also disqualified Balad leader Sami Abu Shehadeh and Hadash MK Ofer Cassif from running. The decisions are set to be challenged at the Supreme Court next week.
A spokesperson for the Joint List told The New Arab that it understood the bans "to be political decisions based on racism against Arab Palestinian citizens and anyone who opposes the Israeli occupation", adding that the list was the only alternative political force in Israel that opposed Israel's occupation of the Palestinian territories and respected international law.
The spokesperson noted that while the initial effort to target the list came from Israel's far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, all Zionist political parties voted alongside him, including the left-wing The Democrats, which has positioned itself as one of the few parties backing a two-state solution.
"This shows the hypocrisy of those who claim to support democracy but are not willing to accept leaders who call for equality," the spokesperson said, adding that "they have shown that they are not a real alternative to the current Israeli government."
The Joint List, which also condemned the banning of Ra'am, is set to challenge the decision in the Supreme Court "as well as in every possible venue, both political and popular".
"We are not going to be intimidated. Our response should include promoting the widest possible participation in the elections on October 27th, making our voices heard no matter the context," the spokesperson added.
No legal grounds for ban
The Legal Center for Arab Minority Rights in Israel (Adalah) is set to contest the disqualification of the political parties and Knesset candidates before the Supreme Court, with Tuesday the deadline for challenging the decisions.
Miriam Azem, Adalah's International Advocacy Coordinator, told The New Arab that the disqualification motions were expected, with Adalah having documented attempts to ban Arab parties and Knesset candidates in numerous Israeli elections, including in 2003, 2013, 2015, 2020 and 2022.
"What surprised us was the position of the Attorney General in the case of Dr. Sami Abu Shehadeh, and the fact that the Committee's chairman, Justice Noam Solhberg, took part in the vote himself," Azem said, noting that this had not happened in the past two decades.
"The Attorney General has taken a completely different route from past Supreme Court precedent. We expected her to state clearly that none of the lists or candidates should be disqualified, and to act as a check on this entirely illegitimate process."
By contrast, Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara, who has repeatedly clashed with the Netanyahu government and fought off an attempt to dismiss her, said that a subsequent effort on Thursday to ban Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit (Jewish Power), far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich's Religious Zionism party and its joint-ticket partner Zehut had no legal basis, according to Haaretz.
Both Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have faced international sanctions over their inflammatory rhetoric and policies towards Palestinians, and have advocated for the displacement of Palestinians from Gaza and the annexation of the occupied West Bank.
Azem said the Arab lists had been disqualified while Israeli far-right lists remained eligible to run, describing the decisions as reflecting a double standard.
"The message to Palestinian citizens is that they may vote, but not for their own leaders, and that their leadership is cast as the enemy," she said.
In the last Knesset, Israeli parties sought to oust two MKs over their staunch criticism of Israel's war on Gaza and occupation of the West Bank: Cassif in 2024 and Ayman Odeh, the former head of Hadash who stepped down ahead of this election, in 2025. Both attempts failed to secure the required supermajority in the Knesset.
There has also been widespread hostility among Israeli Jewish parties towards potential cooperation with Arab parties, despite polling suggesting that neither the pro- nor anti-Netanyahu blocs will hold enough seats to form a government without the support of Arab parties.
"Those who filed them [the motions] believe Arab representatives have no place in the Knesset unless they are Zionist and see Israel the way they do," Azem said.
Looking ahead to the Supreme Court challenge, Azem told The New Arab: "Our case is clear. None of the legal grounds for disqualification is met, and the decisions ignore the Court's precedent, which requires clear and convincing evidence that a disqualification ground is met."
She warned, however, that the current political climate in Israel and pressure on the judiciary meant that previous legal precedent could not be taken for granted.
"Even if the Court overturns them, the damage is done: every election cycle, Arab representatives are forced to prove their legitimacy."

ECB speeches and interviews move markets as much as policy decisions, study finds
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
16:22:15 UTC
01:22:15 KST

Markets react not only to ECB policy decisions but also to policymaker speeches and interviews, whose cumulative impact can rival formal announcements, new research finds.
Speeches and interviews by European Central Bank (ECB) policymakers can move markets as much as formal monetary policy announcements, according to an ECB study published on Thursday.
The research, by economists Klodiana Istrefi, Florens Odendahl and Giulia Sestrieri, found that markets respond not only to the ECB's monetary policy decisions every six weeks, but also to what prominent policymakers say between meetings.
These interventions can shape market expectations about the direction of monetary policy, which in turn affects inflation and unemployment across the euro area.
While the effect may be difficult to detect from an individual speech or interview, the study found that their cumulative impact can be comparable to that of formal policy announcements.
"Our findings show that the market reaction to inter-meeting communication events is often as large as the reaction to formal announcements of Governing Council decisions," the authors wrote in an ECB blog post.
"We also find that inter-meeting communication events can help us better estimate the economic impact of monetary policy in the euro area," they added.
The authors built an "Euro Area Communication Event Study Database" with 304 formal policy decisions and approximately 5,000 public events between January 1999 and early 2024.
They examined speeches and interviews by ECB presidents, board members, and national central bank governors from Germany, France, Spain, and Italy - the four largest euro area countries.
"We found that around 45% of formal policy announcements produced a significant market reaction. By contrast, the results from inter-meeting communication events were more diverse and a smaller share of them generated a significant market reaction," the authors wrote, specifying that the results are not surprising.
"Formal policy announcements following Governing Council meetings are inherently focused on monetary policy decisions, whereas inter-meeting communication events cover a much broader range of topics," they added.
However, such public interventions are far more frequent than formal policy announcements, making their cumulative impact significant.
The study also measured which personalities affect the markets the most in speeches and interviews. In the first place, ECB presidents have "the largest impact on average," followed by national central bank governors, and then by ECB board members.
"This highlights the importance of looking beyond the ECB President and Executive Board members when analysing monetary policy communication in a heterogeneous monetary union, where countries differ significantly in their economic structures, public debt levels, and household and firm financial situations," the report says.

US and Iran discuss phased deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz, end US blockade, sources say
- US and Iranian negotiators are discussing a phased deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the US economic blockade on Iran to ease tensions and economic pressure.
- Both sides face challenges as neither wants to lose leverage, with Iran controlling Hormuz and the US controlling the blockade, making trust and durable concessions crucial.
- Gulf states demand freedom of navigation without Iranian control, while Tehran seeks economic relief; talks risk narrowing post-US midterm elections as military escalation fears persist.
AI generated
NEW YORK - US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased path out of war that would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade of Iran, sources close to the talks said.
The strait has become the central bargaining chip in efforts to end the nearly seven-month US-Iran conflict, with Iran seeking relief from the US blockade that is choking its economy and Washington seeking free passage for ships on the global oil supply route now blocked by Tehran.
The talks face a big obstacle as neither side wants to be the first to surrender its leverage, according to comments to Reuters by two Iranian sources, two regional officials and two Western diplomatic sources, but behind Iran’s stance is a recognition of the economic cost of prolonged confrontation.
A senior Iranian official said the most plausible way to end the impasse would be a phased arrangement, with Iran allowing navigation through Hormuz in return for the US lifting its economic blockade and Tehran potentially gaining access to frozen assets.
“One way forward would be to solve the crisis in stages. The first would be to end the blockade and reopen Hormuz,” he said on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.
That would involve US President Donald Trump accepting another temporary fix, after an earlier understanding collapsed in July. So a central challenge facing the negotiators is not just to sketch out a deal but also to ensure any concessions are durable enough for both sides to trust, the sources said.
Trump has said he thinks the US and Iran could reach a deal after midterm elections to Congress on Nov 3. A senior European official said the Iranians “have a very long list of demands.”
The White House and the US State Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment for this article.
Former US negotiator Dennis Ross said he saw only a 30 per cent chance of an agreement being reached before the vote, but that both sides may have stronger reasons to make a deal before than after the midterms.
“The blockade is what’s really squeezing the Iranians. It’s strangling them,” Ross said.
A deal before the midterms could benefit Trump, as reopening Hormuz could ease tensions in the Gulf, contain oil prices and help bring down politically sensitive US gasoline prices.
Iran’s chances of gaining much-needed economic relief may be greater while Trump still has a greater political incentive to strike a bargain.
After the midterms, Ross said, Trump may face fewer constraints and be more willing to intensify pressure or consider military options.
Leverage as obstacle?
The leverage that brought Washington and Tehran back to negotiations could also make compromise harder.
Washington controls the pressure that is hurting Tehran most, while Tehran controls access to a critical energy chokepoint. Neither side wants to surrender that leverage without extracting something tangible in return.
This means the midterms may be less a deadline for diplomacy than for preserving the conditions that make the diplomatic efforts possible. If Washington and Tehran cannot turn leverage into a deal before the midterms, the diplomatic window could narrow as the risk of escalation grows.
Even as it seeks a diplomatic off-ramp, Tehran is preparing for the possibility of renewed war with Washington, the Iranian official said, accusing the US of using the economic blockade and threat of force as tools of coercion.
“Our fingers are on the trigger,” said the senior Iranian official. “The Americans know what they need to do but, because of their excessive demands, the chances of diplomacy resolving this are extremely low.”
Regional sources said Tehran was willing to drop a demand for payment of transit fees to use the Strait of Hormuz from the main agreement and put the demand in a side attachment instead, as ending the blockade had become the more urgent priority.
Gulf states have rejected the proposal for payment of transit fees. Any arrangement would be temporary, not a formal abandonment of Iran’s position, the regional sources said.
The US has tightened the economic vice on Iran, layering new sanctions on top of a blockade that has choked off Iran’s oil exports, an important source of hard currency.
This month, it targeted Iran’s remaining commercial airlines and support networks as part of a campaign to sever the economic lifelines sustaining the government and the powerful Revolutionary Guards. Trump warned that Iran’s economy could “rot” unless it reached a deal.
“Iran is not primarily focused on imposing tolls in Hormuz but on preserving its administrative control of the waterway,” he said. “Iran may be willing to defer the toll issue, but they are not going to give up administrative control of the strait.”
At the heart of the diplomacy in New York is a fundamental tension. Washington wants pressure to produce concessions, Tehran wants pressure removed before making them, and the Gulf states want the conflict resolved without allowing the region’s strategic waterways to become enduring bargaining chips.
Fears of an open-ended conflict
During a separate meeting with Trump in New York, Gulf leaders sought clarity on Washington’s endgame beyond the midterms, including on whether the US would resume military action if Iran refused to return to negotiations.
They conveyed their collective rejection of any Iranian control of Hormuz, saying freedom of navigation must be restored and that the strategic waterway should not become a tool of coercion against Gulf states, regional sources said.
Yet alongside their warnings over Hormuz, Gulf leaders have pressed hard for de-escalation and a political process, reflecting the region’s determination to stay out of any further conflict between the US and Iran.
“It’s still not clear what Trump’s endgame is, or what the alternative to the pressure campaign would be,” said Ebtessam al-Ketbi, president of the Emirates Policy Centre think-tank based in Abu Dhabi.
“The Iranians, by contrast, know what they want. They’re reshaping the regional landscape through Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb with a clear objective while Washington has yet to define its roadmap,” she said, referring to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait that connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.
That uncertainty is also shaping Tehran’s calculations. Danny Citrinowicz, a regional analyst and former Israeli military intelligence officer, said the New York talks had not altered the basic positions of either side and that Iran was unlikely to retreat as long as it believed Trump wanted to avoid a wider escalation before the midterms.
“The blockade is hurting them, but rather than softening their position, it is likely to drive them to escalate because they believe that if they soften their position, they are dead,” said Alan Eyre, a former US negotiator on Iran.
A Western official familiar with the talks added: “It is all about opening the Strait of Hormuz. We’re all under pressure domestically and the Iranians know that.” REUTERS

01:19:38 KST

The entire housebuilding sector is in a funk, grumbling about energy prices, the cost of labour, regulation, planning delays, taxes and more, but few have messed up a bad hand quite like Vistry. Three years ago this mashup of the Bovis, Linden and Countryside brands aspired to build 20,000 houses a year, and made itself the darling of the incoming Labour government by betting big on “affordable mixed-tenure housing” in partnership with councils, housing associations and institutional landlords.
The City, too, fell for former executive chair Greg Fitzgerald’s promise that a “capital light” approach of pre-selling homes via a partnership model would yield oodles of cash. The share price doubled to almost £14 between October 2023 and August 2024.
Fitzgerald departed in May after too many profit warnings and now, with the shares down to the bare foundations of 262p, it’s time for new chief executive Adam Daniels’ review of what happened. Short version: the logic of the partnership stuff wasn’t so silly, but the execution was horrible, especially in the south of England.
“The pace of change meant that the operating model, controls and culture did not scale consistently with the group’s volumes [of construction],” he said, a polite summary of a growth strategy gone awry. For good measure, a proportion of the land bank would not be acquired “under the investment approval criteria that will be applied in the future”, which read as a confession that Vistry simply overpaid for plots.
The good news, of a sort, for shareholders is that the damage to the balance is not deemed so severe that fresh equity is required. Daniels’ prescription for recovery, however, is a long exercise in getting smaller and living with shrunken ambitions.
The aim is to build 12,000 houses a year, rather than the 20,000-plus imagined by Fitzgerald. A greater proportion of those homes will be in the north of England. As for return on capital employed – a critical metric for housebuilders – the old idea was 40%. That’s been cut to 30%, and only by 2031.
It all sounds perfectly reasonable: keep things simple, fix the balance sheet by eating into the land bank, and concentrate on the parts of the country where market prices (which still matter for a mixed-tenure model) are holding up better.
In Vistry’s favour is the fact that, for all its financial troubles, it’s still in the government’s good books. Last month, the company received a £350m direct grant to construct 3,000 affordable homes under the £39bn social and affordable homes programme. If you take the long view, there is a possibility of a turnaround if Daniels can live up to the promise of better execution. At the age of 35, he has time on his side – and may need it.
The wider message for the government’s target to build 1.5m homes in England during this parliament, however, is as discouraging as ever. Vistry is an extreme example but virtually everybody is reining in ambitions in the name of financial discipline and cash generation. Even Barratt Redrow, the biggest of the lot, said in April it would be scaling back its land purchases. Angela Rayner, the housing secretary, has taken to calling the 1.5m figure a “stretch target”. Indeed, the only real question is by how much it will be missed. By an embarrassing margin, on current form.

MOSCOW, September 24. /TASS/. The minimum wage in Russia will increase by 6.8% in 2027, reaching 28,900 rubles ($340), Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said at a cabinet meeting.
He noted that the federal budget deficit in 2027 would amount to 2.2% of GDP.
The minister stressed that a balanced budget is crucial for maintaining macroeconomic stability, lowering inflation and interest rates, and fostering growth in real disposable household incomes.
TASS has compiled the key statements made by the Finance Minister.
Federal budget
"The budget deficit is set at around 2% of GDP for the coming three years. In 2027, the budget deficit will be 2.2% of GDP."
"Expenditures will total 48.8 trillion rubles ($574 bln), and revenues will amount to 43.3 trillion rubles ($509 bln)."
A balanced budget is important "for maintaining macroeconomic stability, lowering inflation and interest rates, and fostering growth in real disposable household incomes, which will amount to 1.4% next year."
Minimum wage
"The minimum wage in 2027 will be 28,935 rubles--an increase of 6.8%, which reflects the projected wage growth for next year."
"The task set by the President - to raise the minimum wage to 35,000 rubles ($412) by 2030 - will be fulfilled."
Budget policy
"Fostering a competitive environment and fighting the shadow economy is a key objective. This task is part of the plan to formalize economic sectors, including combating 'gray' imports. Consequently, we have factored in additional annual revenues of around 500 billion rubles ($5.8 bln) in the draft budget."
The key principles of tax policy remain in place in the draft federal budget for 2027-2029: "The key principles of tax policy are being maintained: fairness and efficiency."
"The total volume of resources generated through budget optimization will exceed 2 trillion rubles ($23.5 bln) per year."
A total of 520 billion rubles ($6.1 bln) will be allocated for research and development (R&D) and for establishing and equipping production facilities during 2027-2029.
