(China Economic Roundtable) Service consumption outpaces goods as China's consumer market enters new stage: experts
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:12:10 CST
16:12:10 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- China's consumer market has entered a new stage in which goods and services are both important, with service retail sales expanding at nearly five times the pace of goods retail sales in the first eight months of this year, a structural shift captured by a new official indicator in the world's second-largest consumer market.
Total retail sales of consumer goods and services rose 2.5 percent year on year in the January-August period this year, with service retail sales up 4.9 percent and goods retail sales up 1 percent, officials and experts said at the China Economic Roundtable, an all-media talk platform hosted by Xinhua News Agency.
In June this year, the National Bureau of Statistics released the "total retail sales of consumer goods and services" indicator for the first time, a move analysts say better reflects the full picture of consumption as services become an increasingly important driver of domestic demand.
"As per capita income rises, it is an objective economic law that service consumption grows faster than goods consumption," said Lin Jian, vice president of the Chinese Academy of International Trade and Economic Cooperation under the Ministry of Commerce.
The shift is visible in changing consumer behavior. Zhang Weihua, deputy director of the Shandong Provincial Department of Culture and Tourism, said consumers are moving from "buying goods" to "buying peace of mind" and from "functional consumption" to "experiential consumption," seeking immersive, interactive and emotionally rewarding experiences.
For his part, Chen Chunhui, chairman of Xiamen International Cruise Home Port Group Co., Ltd., said that "cruise consumption, from ship to shore, integrates dining, lodging, transport, sightseeing, shopping and entertainment, reflecting the growing demand for composite experiences."
In Xiamen, a coastal city in east China's Fujian Province, the Xiamen International Cruise Home Port, one of China's four pilot demonstration cruise transport ports, saw inbound cruise ship calls rise 33 percent year on year in the first half, with passenger numbers up about 180 percent, according to Chen.
"In the long run, sustainable consumption growth hinges on a virtuous cycle between consumption upgrading and industrial upgrading, with demand-side policies pushing manufacturers toward greener and smarter production," Lin said.
On the policy front, China has been steering demand toward green and smart products through trade-in programs for automobiles and home appliances. The leverage ratio of subsidy funds rose from 1:7.8 in 2025 to 1:10.3 this year, according to Lin.
China is the world's second-largest consumer market. The country targets relatively fast growth in total consumer goods and services consumption, with total retail sales of consumer goods reaching around 60 trillion yuan (about 8.3 trillion U.S. dollars) by 2030. It also aims to cultivate 10-trillion-yuan-level markets in green, intelligent and health-related consumption.
China also aims to attract 190 million inbound tourist visits a year by 2030, with annual inbound tourism spending exceeding 150 billion U.S. dollars, according to a new five-year tourism development plan unveiled in July this year. The plan signals the country's expanding efforts to draw overseas visitors as it seeks to boost consumption.
Lin said new growth areas such as "AI plus consumption" are expected to expand rapidly, providing broad space for the upgrading of goods and services consumption.
"Service consumption and goods consumption will become more deeply integrated, with their boundaries increasingly blurred. But what remains unchanged is starting from user demand and continuously turning real needs into products," said Zhang Dandan, head of the Changsha New Consumption Research Institute.
"During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), China's service consumption is expected to accelerate further," Lin added. ■

Economic Watch: NEV industry on fast track in south China's Hainan
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:12:08 CST
16:12:08 KST

HAIKOU, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- The new energy vehicle (NEV) industry is on a fast track in south China's Hainan, as the tropical island province leverages advantages to advance intelligent connected vehicles.
As China's first province to set the goal of banning the sale of combustion-engine cars by 2030, Hainan has remained at the forefront of the country's NEV promotion.
In the first eight months of this year, Hainan's NEV penetration rate reached 66.1 percent, ranking first in China, while NEVs accounted for 25.7 percent of the province's vehicle ownership, ranking second nationwide, Hainan's governor Liu Xiaoming said at the 2026 World New Energy Vehicle Congress, held in the provincial capital Haikou from Sept. 22 to 24.
Leveraging free trade port policies, Hainan is accelerating the development of its auto industry by extending preferential policies to the sector. So far, several special-purpose vehicle projects have been launched in Hainan, and modified special-purpose vehicles have been exported in batches.
Behind the robust NEV development in Hainan is a wider trend. Data showed that during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025), China's NEV industry grew rapidly, with sales reaching 16.49 million units in 2025. The average annual growth rate reached 65 percent from 2020 to 2025.
In September this year, China issued a development plan for intelligent connected NEVs, focusing on core fields such as vehicle-road-cloud integration.
"China's auto industry has developed clear advantages, particularly in electrification and intelligent technologies," said Yu Zhuoping, a professor at Tongji University and an expert with the Hainan New Energy Vehicle Industry International Expert Advisory Committee.
Hainan laid a solid foundation for the development of intelligent NEVs at an early stage. From 2021 to 2022, it built a provincial NEV data monitoring platform, which has connected nearly 600,000 NEVs to date. In 2024, the cities of Haikou, Sanya and Qionghai were selected as a national pilot region for vehicle-road-cloud integration. Hainan's latest five-year plan from 2026 to 2030 also identifies innovative AI in transportation as a key direction.
"Hainan has three unique core advantages for comprehensively advancing province-wide intelligent connectivity of vehicles," Yu said. "First, Hainan's closed island terrain and independent, complete road network make the operational space for vehicles controllable, thus making the island naturally suited to unified and standardized intelligent traffic management."
He added that the Hainan Free Trade Port can pilot institutional innovation in cross-border data flows, market access and rules, providing an excellent testbed for breakthroughs in the intelligent connected vehicle industry.
"Hainan's high NEV penetration and large-scale vehicle ownership also provide a solid application base for technology iteration, scenario implementation and data accumulation," Yu added.
More policies are yet to come.
Governor Liu said that Hainan will focus on special-purpose vehicle manufacturing and the intelligent connected vehicle industry, and promote coordinated development of specialty-vehicle manufacturing, professional supporting services and intelligent innovative applications.
Hainan will "strive to build a global hub for intelligent connected NEV manufacturing and overseas services, so as to contribute to China's auto industry transformation and upgrade toward intelligence and internationalization," Liu added. ■

64 pct of Sri Lankan preschool children exceed recommended screen time: official
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:12:07 CST
16:12:07 KST

COLOMBO, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- About 64 percent of preschool children in Sri Lanka spend more than 30 minutes a day using mobile phones, tablets or computers, Health Ministry Secretary Anil Jasinghe said on Thursday.
Jasinghe said the World Health Organization recommends that young children spend less than 30 minutes a day using digital screens.
A survey by the ministry also found that around 43 percent eat meals while watching a screen.
Jasinghe said the survey also highlighted concerns about caregiving, with around 56 percent of parents or preschool caregivers reporting that they become angry with children.
He said fathers were less involved in childcare, with only about 53 percent closely engaged in caring for their children.
The Health Ministry has introduced a health promotion program and guidelines for preschool children in response to the findings, Jasinghe said. ■

Afghanistan breaks ground on 30-mln-USD pharmaceutical plant in Kandahar
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:11:59 CST
16:11:59 KST

KABUL, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- Afghan authorities inaugurated construction of a major pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in southern Kandahar province on Wednesday, a step toward industrial self-reliance and reduced dependence on imported medicines, the provincial government office said in a statement.
Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony, Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar underscored the strategic importance of expanding domestic industry.
"Economic independence and self-sufficiency can only be achieved through comprehensive and decisive measures in the industrial sector," he said, adding that the country has now created favorable conditions for investment.
The privately financed plant, budgeted at 30 million U.S. dollars, will rise on a 10,000-square-meter site in the Ayno Maina area of Kandahar city, the provincial capital, according to the statement released on Wednesday.
Official data indicate that Afghanistan currently operates 134 pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities, producing 1,170 different medicines. These plants meet roughly 38 percent of the nation's total pharmaceutical demand. ■

China Focus: China's extended holiday set to boost long-haul travel, border crossings
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:11:41 CST
16:11:41 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- China's upcoming Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays bring travelers a major bonus this year: extra time for longer journeys and extended stays.
Separated by three working days, the three-day and seven-day holiday periods can be bridged into a 13-day break running from Sept. 25 to Oct. 7.
REACHING FAROFF DESTINATIONS
For Shanghai white-collar worker Zheng Bing, the extended break means she can leave before the Mid-Autumn Festival, which falls on Sept. 25 per the lunar calendar, and spend more time in Malaysia.
"This allows me to enjoy my vacation at a leisurely pace," said Zheng, whose plans mirror a wider desire for long-haul travel over the coming holiday.
Data from Chinese online travel platforms show that tours of 10 days or more are particularly popular, making up 26 percent of all bookings. Meanwhile, flight reservations for top international destinations have surged over 20 percent year on year.
"Sales for international packages with stays over 10 days are up from last year," said Wang Wei, president of the Shanghai-based Spring International Travel Service (Group) Co., Ltd.
Popular spots include Spain, Greece, Britain, Türkiye and Azerbaijan, the firm added.
China's National Immigration Administration expects an average of about 2.25 million cross-border trips per day during the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday from Sept. 25 to 27, and about 2.15 million per day during the National Day holiday from Oct. 1 to 7.
Sales of tour packages to domestic long-haul destinations are also gaining momentum. On Fliggy, Alibaba Group's online travel platform, reservations to such destinations, including Urumqi in northwest China's Xinjiang, Kunming in southwest Yunnan, and Sanya in the far southern island province of Hainan, have been on the rise.
Flight ticket bookings confirm this trend. According to data from Umetrip, a mobile platform for real-time flight information, the number of reservations for domestic flights flying over 2,000 km surpassed 1.74 million, a year-on-year increase of 14 percent.
EXPERIENCES OUTWEIGH CHECKLIST TOURS
Analysts said that more tourists are favoring special travel experiences, niche tourist destinations and customized packages, particularly when the upcoming super-long holiday makes such travel plans easier to enjoy.
"For younger tourists, how to spend a vacation matters more than where to spend it," said Yang Han, a researcher with online travel platform Qunar.
In the upcoming holidays, bookings for glacier hiking on Fliggy went up 50 percent from the previous year, skydiving up nearly 80 percent, and whale watching surged 200 percent.
Niche tourist destinations, such as lesser-known county-level towns, are attracting tourists. Online travel platform Tongcheng predicted that tourists will stay 3.2 days longer in county-level destinations on average compared with the same period last year.
Tourists are also discovering new sides of cities and towns beyond their famous landmarks or cultural heritage. On online travel platforms, hotel bookings and ticket reservations have surged in cities hosting concerts, sporting events and cultural activities.
QUALITY TOUR PACKAGES IN DEMAND
As more tourists opt for immersive, in-depth experiences rather than hurried sightseeing, they are also on the hunt for better accommodation and higher-quality travel services.
A longer holiday creates more room for tourism consumption, said Cheng Chaogong at Tongcheng. "Quality and experience will become key factors," Cheng noted.
The government is also on the move to make sure diverse cultural events and spending incentives are in place across the country.
China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism launched a month-long national tourism promotion campaign on Sept. 22. While hosting more than 20,000 events spanning scenic trips, autumn outings, red tourism, study tours, night activities and local food to boost diverse premium tourism offerings, local governments are handing out some 310 million yuan (about 45.9 million U.S. dollars) in consumer vouchers and subsidies over the month as a way to spur tourism consumption.
Zheng is about to leave for Malaysia tonight. She's eagerly anticipating her unhurried but fulfilling holiday. "I could still have time to take a rest and check the air of festivity in Shanghai after the trip," she said. ■

KATHMANDU, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- A Sita Air aircraft carrying 13 passengers from Nepalgunj lost its rear tyre while landing at Juphal Airport in Nepal's western Dolpa district on Thursday morning, police said.
The aircraft, with the call sign 9N-AJH, was landing at around 8:25 a.m. local time when the tyre came off.
"All passengers are safe and no injuries have been reported," Anil Raj Giri, chief of the Dolpa district police, told Xinhua. Of the total, seven of the passengers were foreign nationals.
The aircraft remained on the runway following the incident, preventing other aircraft from landing at Juphal Airport.
Authorities are assessing the situation and working to clear the runway, according to Giri. ■

Pakistan launches precision airstrikes on Afghanistan following thwarted drone attack from border
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
07:03:29 UTC
16:03:29 KST

Pakistan conducted airstrikes on 10 locations in Afghanistan that it said were being used to launch and store drones, some of which had been used against Pakistan a day earlier, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Thursday.
The strikes come as tensions escalate between the allies-turned-foes, who have long been at odds over attacks by Islamist militants, which also triggered their worst fighting in years in February.
Islamabad accuses Kabul of harboring militants who stage cross-border attacks, but Afghanistan's Taliban government denies harboring anti-Pakistani insurgents and says militancy is Pakistan's internal problem.
Pakistan's air defense systems detected drones launched from Afghan territory on Wednesday, which were tracked and neutralized before they could reach any of their intended targets, Tarar said in a post on X/Twitter.
Pakistan then conducted the "precision aerial and drone strikes" on 10 locations, which were "limited to identified military objectives" linked to the attempted attacks, he said.
Afghan Taliban will be met with 'firm and resolute response'
"Any further provocative act by Afghan Taliban will be responded with firm and resolute response," the minister said.
The Pakistani airstrikes were conducted in several areas of the southeastern Khost province, Mustaghfir Gurbaz, spokesperson for the Khost governor, said.
There were no casualties, he said. However, a Taliban spokesperson said that four were killed in the strikes.
An attack on a police facility in northwestern Pakistan last week, which killed at least 24 people, has reignited fighting between the countries after nearly three months of relative calm.
Pakistan's government earlier this week also said it had launched airstrikes in the Afghanistan-Pakistan border region, killing 28 militants, while Afghan Taliban officials accused Islamabad of killing three civilians in overnight strikes on Afghan territory.
The worst single incident, however, occurred in March, when more than 400 people were killed in a Pakistani airstrike on Kabul, which the Afghan Taliban said hit a drug rehabilitation center.
Islamabad denied the charge, saying it "precisely targeted military installations and terrorist support infrastructure."

Shutdown in Ladakh on anniversary of deadly protest
Residents in India's Ladakh region observed a shutdown in the city of Leh on Thursday, marking a year since four people were killed when security forces opened fire during protests demanding greater autonomy.
Shops and businesses remained closed and streets were largely deserted, witnesses said. Buddhist groups also organised prayers to commemorate those they called "martyrs."
"The shutdown is to commemorate those who laid down their lives for Ladakh and express solidarity with their families, and... to highlight our demands for autonomy," a member of the Ladakh Buddhist Association told AFP
Last year on September 24, security forces opened fire as demonstrations turned violent in the sparsely populated Himalayan region.
The protests stem from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government's decision in 2019 to end Ladakh's semi-autonomous status.
Residents say the move weakened protections for local land, jobs, resources and cultural identity.

CJP targets Gyanesh Kumar over SIR, alleges voter deletions benefit BJP
Cockroach Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke has accused India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of undermining the country's democracy and alleged that the Election Commission's voter-roll revision is being used to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Speaking at a press conference on Thursday, Dipke called Kumar "the biggest threat to India's democracy" and demanded his resignation.
CJP said it would launch protests across the country if India's chief election officer does not resign in 48 hours.
The CJP's demands are:
- Initiate criminal proceedings against Kumar
- All upcoming elections put on hold, freeze Special Intensive Revision (SIR)
- Repeal the 2023 law on the appointment of the Election Commissioners of India
Kumar overruled fellow election commissioners' concerns
Dipke's accusations came after the Indian Express published an investigation that fellow Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised at least 14 formal objections over 10 months to decisions concerning voter registrations, deletions and restorations, as well as control of electoral-roll data, the report said.
In one of the objections, Sandhu complained that the Election Commission acted against the written advice of two commissioners and claimed its action was "unauthorized and illegal."
Sandhu and Joshi, along with Kumar, are responsible for overseeing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). The process is meant to remove redundancies in India's electoral rolls, but the process is accused of having gone far beyond that remit and removed millions of legal voters.
According to the Election Commission, the revision was needed to remove the names of deceased individuals, those who have permanently moved and duplicate entries — as well as avoiding the "inclusion of the names of foreign illegal immigrants."
'Kumar's actions benefit BJP'
Dipke alleged that more than 130 million names have been struck off draft electoral rolls across 30 states and union territories during the SIR process.
Dipke alleged the removals from voter registries were intended to widen the BJP's electoral advantage as voter deletions had disproportionately affected opposition strongholds.
Dipke pointed out that during the 2024 election the difference in total votes between the ruling party and the opposition coalition was 2%.
"Deleting 130 million votes means deleting approximately 13 to 14 percent of the votes," Dipke said. "So, is Gyanesh Kumar intentionally deleting them so that the two-percent gap, where it appears that the BJP could lose, becomes larger, so that they never have to leave power?"
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also alleged earlier that the SIR process benefits the BJP. The ruling party has dismissed such claims, arguing that those removed largely involve dead voters and illegal immigrants, thereby protecting India's democracy.
Three arrested over alleged gang rape of 17-year-old girl in New Delhi
Authorities have arrested three men accused gang-raping a 17-year-old girl in southeast Delhi.
The girl had been visiting a temple with a male friend on Monday evening before the two went to a nearby park, where the suspects allegedly intercepted them. The men posed as police officers to intimidate the minor and her friend.
One of the men reportedly restrained the girl's friend while the other two assaulted her.
The suspects allegedly threatened the pair with arrest if they reported the incident, according to police cited by The Hindustan Times.
On Wednesday, hundreds of students protested in Delhi, demanding better safety for women. The alleged assault occurred barely 2 km (1.2 miles) from Lady Shri Ram (LSR) College, one of the country's top women's colleges.

An investigation team probing the alleged embezzlement of donations and offerings at the Ram Temple in the northern city of Ayodhya has filed a chargesheet against eight arrested suspects, media reports said on Wednesday.
The police filed a 74,000-page chargesheet before a local court. All eight accused are in judicial custody.
The Special Investigation Team's (SIT) status report documented 105 instances of theft captured by CCTV cameras at the temple premises.
The controversy over alleged embezzlement forced authorities to appoint an Indian Air Force veteran, Jeetendra Mishra, as the chief executive officer of the temple earlier this month.

It built at the site of the Babri mosque, which was demolished by Hindu nationalist mobs in 1992.
Devout Hindus believe that the god Ram was born there more than 7,000 years ago, but that the Babri mosque was built over his birthplace by a 16th-century Muslim emperor.

Shutdown in Ladakh on anniversary of deadly protest
Residents in India's Ladakh region observed a shutdown in the city of Leh on Thursday, marking a year since four people were killed when security forces opened fire during protests demanding greater autonomy.
Shops and businesses remained closed and streets were largely deserted, witnesses said. Buddhist groups also organised prayers to commemorate those they called "martyrs."

Residents say the move weakened protections for local land, jobs, resources and cultural identity.

CJP targets Gyanesh Kumar over SIR, alleges voter deletions benefit BJP
Cockroach Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke has accused India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of undermining the country's democracy and alleged that the Election Commission's voter-roll revision is being used to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Speaking at a press conference on Thursday, Dipke called Kumar "the biggest threat to India's democracy" and demanded his resignation.
CJP said it would launch protests across the country if India's chief election officer does not resign in 48 hours.
The CJP's demands are:
- Initiate criminal proceedings against Kumar
- All upcoming elections put on hold, freeze Special Intensive Revision (SIR)
- Repeal the 2023 law on the appointment of the Election Commissioners of India
Kumar overruled fellow election commissioners' concerns
Dipke's accusations came after the Indian Express published an investigation that fellow Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised at least 14 formal objections over 10 months to decisions concerning voter registrations, deletions and restorations, as well as control of electoral-roll data, the report said.
In one of the objections, Sandhu complained that the Election Commission acted against the written advice of two commissioners and claimed its action was "unauthorized and illegal."
Sandhu and Joshi, along with Kumar, are responsible for overseeing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). The process is meant to remove redundancies in India's electoral rolls, but the process is accused of having gone far beyond that remit and removed millions of legal voters.
According to the Election Commission, the revision was needed to remove the names of deceased individuals, those who have permanently moved and duplicate entries — as well as avoiding the "inclusion of the names of foreign illegal immigrants."
'Kumar's actions benefit BJP'
Dipke alleged that more than 130 million names have been struck off draft electoral rolls across 30 states and union territories during the SIR process.
Dipke alleged the removals from voter registries were intended to widen the BJP's electoral advantage as voter deletions had disproportionately affected opposition strongholds.
Dipke pointed out that during the 2024 election the difference in total votes between the ruling party and the opposition coalition was 2%.
"Deleting 130 million votes means deleting approximately 13 to 14 percent of the votes," Dipke said. "So, is Gyanesh Kumar intentionally deleting them so that the two-percent gap, where it appears that the BJP could lose, becomes larger, so that they never have to leave power?"
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also alleged earlier that the SIR process benefits the BJP. The ruling party has dismissed such claims, arguing that those removed largely involve dead voters and illegal immigrants, thereby protecting India's democracy.

Netflix’s A Different World Revival Has Less Spark But Loads of Heart
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
07:00:03 UTC
16:00:03 KST

Hillman College might be the most vividly realized institution of higher learning that never cashed an actual tuition check. The fictional historically Black college at the heart of A Different World, the generation-defining NBC sitcom that ran for six seasons beginning in 1987, has school colors (maroon and white) and a Latin motto (“Deus nondum te confecit,” or “God is not done with you yet”). It has sports teams, Greek organizations, homecoming traditions. The campus is constantly abuzz, with political debates animating common rooms and flirtations heating up over comfort food at Hillman’s hangout of choice, The Pit. But what really makes the school is its people—Black teens from every conceivable background forging lifelong friendships under the empathetic eyes of adults committed to helping them thrive and mature.
Which is why, even as the TV of the ’80s and ’90s is strip-mined for blandly familiar streaming content, Hillman feels like a place worth revisiting. Also titled A Different World, Netflix’s just-released revival does precisely that in a 10-episode dramedy set among Gen Z freshmen. Yet it also maintains a strong connection to the past, re-enlisting as an executive producer and director Debbie Allen, the architect of the series’ greatness, and making its protagonist the daughter of the opposites-attract golden couple Dwayne Wayne (Kadeem Hardison) and Whitley Gilbert-Wayne (Jasmine Guy). The new episodes don’t have quite the same spark of energy and wit that made the original a classic; stylistically, they share more with contemporary teen dramas like the HBCU-set All American: Homecoming and the straight-faced Fresh Prince reboot Bel-Air, whose writer and producer Felicia Pride helms this sequel. But the show does share with its predecessor vibrant characters, appealing performances, and a keen sense of how the personal intersects with the political. It’s more than enough to justify the return trip.
Relatable like her dad, a brilliant mathematician from pre-gentrification Brooklyn, but also entitled like her posh Southern belle mom, Maleah Joi Moon’s Deborah Wayne makes an ideal ingénue, prone to frustrating choices yet still somehow charming. She’s the ultimate Hillman legacy; not only are her parents both grads, but Dwayne is now provost and Whitley (a beauty mogul, to no one’s surprise) is as involved in the alumni scene as you’d expect the namesake of Gilbert Hall to be. So this freshman grew up with campus fixtures like Prof. Freddie Brooks (Cree Summer, reprising her role as Hillman’s resident social justice crusader) and Pit proprietor Nellie Gaines (Famecia Ward, playing the granddaughter of the late Lou Myers’s beloved character, Vernon Gaines). Along with satisfying the nostalgia of longtime fans, these relationships give the show access to the high-stakes higher-ed bureaucracy students rarely glimpse. It’s an effective setup, although a plot that puts the Waynes’ marriage in peril, calling back to their will-they-or-won’t-they courtship, doesn’t feel entirely earned, let alone necessary.
Really, though, the new Different World is about the kids. And that’s as it should be. As with the original cast, the mix of personalities and backstories is key. Deborah has unfinished business—of the romantic sort, naturally—with Shaquille (Cornell Young IV), the football-star son of her dad’s old roommate, smooth schemer Ron Johnson (Darryl M. Bell). Despite being second-generation Hillmanites, neither is sure they truly belong there. Shaquille had Division 1 teams fighting over him but opted to make a statement by playing for an HBCU instead. An aspiring artist whose wild behavior ruined her chances at NYU, Deborah had no alternative.
Her inner circle includes roommate Rashida Duvall (Alijah Kai, another standout), a driven scholarship student who calls herself “the Simone Biles of school” and whose eventual bond with Deborah echoes Whitley’s odd-couple friendship with her own Hillman roommate, Kim (Charnele Brown, who also guest stars). Hazel Henry (Kennedi Reece), whose church-girl innocence belies big ambitions, completes the trio. Among Shaquille’s boys are Kojo Achebe (Chibuikem Uche), whose aspirations of becoming a fashion designer don’t exactly thrill his strict African parents, and Amir Rodale (Jordan Aaron Hall), a formerly incarcerated student whose time in juvie continues to interfere with his life at Hillman. Amir is also the franchise’s first gay main character, an identity that Hall and the writers navigate with grace and ease.
It’s a reverent reinvention, one that the people behind the first Different World clearly support. (Jada Pinkett Smith, Joe Morton, Glynn Turman, and Jenifer Lewis are just a few of the other past stars who appear.) Without defaulting to the Very Special Episodes that worked better in primetime than they do in a binge-dropped streaming season, Pride engages with issues relevant to her young, Black characters, often letting themes develop across episodes. Allen’s groundbreaking storylines about apartheid protests, AIDS, and the censorship of rap lyrics have given way to ones that consider the stigma around learning disabilities, friction between African and Black American cultures, and HBCUs’ reliance on funding from an anti-DEI federal government. In one episode, a bomb threat forces students to realize the school they’d hoped would give them a four-year reprieve from racism is also uniquely vulnerable to it. Yet, true to its history, the show thoughtfully interweaves these topical beats into collegiate lives that revolve around schoolwork, romantic mess, friend-group drama, money troubles, dreams of the future.
The real divergence between the two visions of Hillman is in tone. Once it got past a first season weighed down by its connection, via Lisa Bonet’s original lead, Denise Huxtable, to The Cosby Show and its since-disgraced creator, not to mention the odd gimmick of casting Marisa Tomei as Denise’s white roommate, A Different World was lightning in a bottle. Allen used the jaunty spirit of sitcoms and outsize characters like Whitley and Ron to create 23-minute, multicam stage plays funny, dynamic, and daring enough to make viewers forget that our perspective on Hillman was confined to a handful of dorm-room and common-space interiors. Thanks in part to a talented cast who went on to become fixtures of movies and TV, and in part to the optimism of a post-civil-rights generation that, for all its many challenges, had reason to believe progress would continue, it was possible to spotlight injustice and do pratfalls and lovers’ tiffs in the same scene. Whitley and Dwayne were honeymooning in LA when the Rodney King verdict came down! Roseanne and Tom Arnold, of all people, guest-starred as white looters. (Susan Fales-Hill, then the head writer, has said she thinks the episode sealed the show’s cancellation.)
Pride was probably wise not to try recreating that balance of serious and silly. It might have come off as trivializing to a generation raised amid bigoted, post-Obama backlash and choose-your-own-apocalypse visions of doom within their lifetimes. Even if it didn’t, the multicam sitcom, in its current incarnations as well as its classic ones, reads as a throwback. The decision not to coast on nostalgia, to give viewers access to a fully realized, if somewhat more somber Hillman of classrooms and quads and athletic fields and libraries, is a sound one. More lamentable, yet also understandable, is the extent to which principled preaching, often by respected elders, supplants the hearty debate among characters that once served to underscore the diversity of thought within the Black community. The original series combined an ideal cast with ideal scripts, at precisely the right time to see them embraced by tens of millions of fans. It can’t be reproduced. Thirty-three years later, we have A Different World for a truly different world, though not the one a newly married Dwayne and Whitley might have hoped for.

An advocate for the laws of war in a world that no longer believes in them
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
07:00:00 UTC
16:00:00 KST

An advocate for the laws of war in a world that no longer believes in them
Alain Délétroz’s job involves meeting with warlords to convince them to protect civilians. As director general of the NGO Geneva Call, Délétroz pursues this mission even as the United States and other countries set an increasingly poor example.
Alain Délétroz, 190cm tall, has the ideal stature for his unusual work: encountering some of the most ruthless armed groups on the planet to raise their awareness of the laws of war. His intense gaze compels attention, but his calm, measured voice and affability reveal a profound humanism and sensitivity.
Swissinfo met with him recently to discuss his career. Although he has travelled the world, he remains true to his roots in canton Valais and offered us coffee and Swiss chocolate while we spoke.
When asked what led him, in 2017, to accept his current post, he replied: “From a very young age, I’ve been drawn to what makes humans remain human even in the worst circumstances.” His unshakeable “faith in humanity”, he explained, evolved from his Catholic upbringing and propelled him into humanitarian work. He began his career in 1994 as an International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) delegate in Moscow.
“What struck me in my various jobs, especially during my first years as a young delegate, was seeing that this spark of humanity can be found in the hearts of people who have committed the worst crimes,” he said. “In fact, that is what Geneva Call works on.”
In sensitising armed groups to the Geneva Conventions that define the laws of war, the NGO originally aimed to fill a gap in the humanitarian sector. A quarter-century later, Geneva Call has established itself as a key player among Geneva’s international organisations. It is also one of the most discreet, although Délétroz willingly let Swissinfo peek behind the curtain.
Spark of humanity
Today, Geneva Call is in contact with more than 200 armed groups scattered across the globe. Approaching them and gaining their trust requires a thorough understanding of local circumstances, so over the last ten years the organisation has developed a network of field offices.
“It’s no longer staff from the Geneva headquarters who [fly in] to initiate dialogue. Our local colleagues do this work,” Délétroz explained. He then joins them later, when there is an opportunity to meet with high-ranking commanders.
How does he manage to convince warlords, with whom he seemingly has nothing in common, to respect international humanitarian law that is alien to them? “A purely legal argument is insufficient, in itself, to bring about a change in behaviour by armed groups that have committed, sometimes for years, serious violence against civilian populations,” he said. “You have to find something else.”
This “something else” is precisely the “spark of humanity” that Délétroz referred to throughout our meeting. “You have to try to find the thing that, in their mental framework or ideology, allows you to forge a connection,” he said. But he clarified that there is “no formula”.
His mastery of languages, including Quechua (which he learned as a young man from indigenous Peruvians) and Russian, surely is an enormous asset. So is his deep faith, which he has maintained throughout his life, and which he nourished as a seminarian for two years in the Spiritan missionary religious congregation within the Catholic Church.
Délétroz emphasises the importance of cultural and religious factors for these armed groups, which are invariably pursuing what he called “a cause”.
“If you question it, it’s over. Obviously, when I arrive in certain conflict [zones], as a [civilian], it is difficult for me to convince myself that their cause is just,” he admitted. But humanitarian neutrality allows him to set aside political considerations. “We don’t discuss the reasons people are fighting each other, but rather the way in which they are doing this and their responsibility towards civilian populations.”
This can lead to interactions that, to an outside observer, might seem surprising or even shocking. “I was recently on the phone discussing a delicate matter with a commander no one would describe as gentle. At the end of our conversation, he told me, ‘You and I share the same values’,” Délétroz said with an embarrassed laugh. But his job, by definition, is to speak with everyone.
When he describes his many trips to war zones – recently, for example, to the Democratic Republic of the Congo and soon to Ukraine and the Middle East – Délétroz carefully avoids naming his interlocutors. But this does not stop him from speaking more frankly than is typical in the discreet world of Geneva’s international organisations.
More
Cambodia’s Tun Channareth renews fight for mine-free world in Geneva
Erosion of international humanitarian law
The mission of Geneva Call has perhaps never been as difficult as it is today. It is challenging to convince armed groups to respect the Geneva Conventions when party states aren’t doing so themselves.
“Not a single national army engaged in combat is behaving properly,” Délétroz observed bitterly. He laments the widespread “erosion of international humanitarian law” in places as varied as Ukraine, Gaza, and Sudan.
“Since the Israeli bombardments of Gaza, several commanders of armed groups in the Middle East have told us very clearly: ‘Don’t talk to us about the Geneva Conventions anymore. If such horror can happen before our eyes without anyone caring, why should we respect these laws?’,” Délétroz said.
His teams therefore have to look elsewhere for ideas – in the codes of conduct of other militias or in religious texts that advocate similar rules.
“Contrary to what you might think, the vast majority of these groups wish to keep talking,” Délétroz was keen to point out. He nonetheless acknowledges that certain groups, notably jihadists, reject any kind of dialogue.
From his office overlooking the main United Nations square in Geneva, Délétroz has also noted that the nature of conflicts is evolving. “The biggest change in the last ten years is the area on the map of the world controlled by armed groups,” he said. This has expanded significantly and now encompasses over 200 million people. Certain militias have become de facto authorities that administer entire territories.
These changes have also transformed the work of his organisation, which currently has an annual budget of roughly CHF20 million ($25 million). “Initially, we focused mainly on the behaviour of combatants,” Délétroz said. “Today, we also offer training in the management and protection of civilian populations.”
Remaining hopeful
We asked Délétroz whether, after ten years of this work, he has any specific regrets. He thought for a moment. “When I saw the footage of October 7th, I said to myself that we had made a mistake in not engaging in dialogue with Hamas,” he said, “because none of the groups we work with kill civilians with garden tools.”
Geneva Call had never approached the Palestinian movement as many other humanitarian organisations were already active in the Middle East. The NGO had therefore chosen to focus its efforts on other conflicts, particularly in Africa.
At 62, Délétroz, father of two sons and three daughters, refuses to give way to pessimism despite the erosion of international humanitarian law, a deteriorating security environment, and the funding crisis in the humanitarian sector.
“What motivates me is seeing people who used to commit crimes change their behaviour, establish rules for their troops, and punish violations,” Délétroz said. “This is what gives us the strength to continue.”

Architects: THINK TANK architecture
- Area: 81500 m²
Text description provided by the architects. The new Zando Central Market of Kinshasa, was conceived above all as an African market, not a mall. Despite its scale and thanks to the attention to comfort, the project remains open to the city, its climate, its people and its everyday life. North Korea tests a guided rocket built like America’s GMLRS
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
06:58:06 UTC
15:58:06 KST

- North Korea test-fired an upgraded, guided 240mm rocket on Sept. 22 that it says can strike targets up to 115 km away, threatening the Seoul area.
- The guided rocket is separate from North Korea's older, unguided 240mm launchers already supplied to Russia for use against Ukraine.
North Korea test-fired an upgraded, precision-guided 240mm rocket on Sept. 22, state media said Sept. 24, claiming the new round can strike targets up to 115 km (71 miles) away, close enough to reach the Seoul metropolitan area from launch positions north of the Demilitarized Zone. North Korea has built the rocket along the same basic concept as the U.S. Army’s GMLRS, the guided rocket fired from HIMARS: take a large-caliber artillery rocket and add a guidance package so it can hit a specific point rather than simply saturating an area.
GMLRS, short for Guided Multiple Launch Rocket System, is the precision rocket the U.S. Army fires from HIMARS, trading the wide dispersal of older unguided rockets for a satellite-guided system that can hit a specific point target dozens of kilometers away. North Korea’s new 240mm rocket follows the same basic concept: take an existing large-caliber artillery rocket and add a guidance package so it can be aimed rather than simply launched en masse.
The Korean Central News Agency said the test was part of North Korea’s five-year defense development plan and involved what it called an “updated 240mm guided rocket.” The agency said the rocket uses an onboard precision guidance system and can reach 100 km (62 miles) on a standard ballistic trajectory, or up to 115 km using a combined glide-and-ballistic flight path, a range and flight profile that puts it in the same general class as extended-range versions of GMLRS.
This guided rocket is a distinct weapon from North Korea’s older 240mm multiple rocket launcher, sometimes called the M1991 by Western analysts, which fires unguided, spin-stabilized rockets in mass salvos with a range of roughly 40 to 60 km. North Korea has supplied that older, unguided system to Russia for use against Ukraine. Ukrainian intelligence and open-source reporting have documented North Korean M1991 launchers, along with M-1989 self-propelled howitzers and ballistic missiles, transferred to Russian forces since late 2024, and Russian troops have used the rockets on the battlefield in Ukraine, according to footage geolocated by Ukrainian military journalists.
North Korea first tested a guided version of the 240mm rocket in May 2024, then tested an upgraded variant again on May 26, 2026, alongside two other systems: an AI-guided tactical cruise missile and a separate, lightweight rocket launcher that Western analysts have compared to HIMARS itself, distinct from the 240mm rocket program. That HIMARS-style launcher first appeared publicly at a 2023 military parade, and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected it moving toward production during a factory tour Sept. 16 to 18, according to state media.
South Korea’s military has previously tracked North Korean weapons tests independently, though it has not always confirmed Pyongyang’s specific performance claims, and Seoul has not yet issued its own assessment of the Sept. 22 guided rocket test or the range figures North Korea reported.

Severe weather caused CHF60m Swiss crop damage
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

Severe weather caused CHF60m Swiss crop damage
The summer drought and hail storms caused CHF59.2 million in crop damage, according to agricultural insurer Hagel Schweiz. This is almost three times as much damage as last summer.
The months of April to August were the driest and hottest since records began in 1901 and led to significant crop failures, said Hagel Schweiz. The insurance company expects 5,800 claims for the current year.
The drought was responsible for 45% of the claims, while hail accounts for 48%. “This year’s drought clearly shows just how much agriculture is already suffering from the effects of climate change,” said Hagel Switzerland.
Summer crops such as potatoes, maize, sugar beet and sunflowers were particularly hard hit. Due to the high compensation payments, Hagel Switzerland also expects a significantly negative operating result.

EBRD forecasts 3 percent growth for Türkiye in 2026
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
06:53:33 UTC
15:53:33 KST

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) expects Türkiye’s economy to grow by 3 per cent in 2026, down from a 3.5 per cent forecast made in June 2026.
Growth is projected to accelerate to 4 per cent in 2027.
These forecasts were published on Sept. 24 in the Bank’s latest Regional Economic Prospects (REP) report.
The downward revision reflects weaker domestic demand amid high inflation and tight financial conditions, as well as the continuing impact of the conflict in the Middle East and cost competitiveness pressures on exports, the bank said.
The REP states that an escalation of hostilities in the Middle East could put further pressure on energy prices, reduce tourism revenues, trigger capital outflows and disrupt trade. In addition, growing foreign-exchange liabilities expose corporate balance sheets to lira depreciation, it warned.
On the upside, a lasting peace in the Middle East, stronger external demand and continued policy discipline could support investment and faster growth, it said.
Aggregate growth across the EBRD regions is projected at 2.5 per cent in 2026 before accelerating to 4 per cent in 2027.
The 2026 forecast was revised down by 0.6 percentage points since June, reflecting tighter financing conditions, the impact of drought across parts of Europe and the Black Sea blockade related to Russia’s continued invasion of Ukraine, the bank said.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) – More than 80% of Taiwanese consider China’s gray-zone activities a serious threat to national security, according to a poll by the Taiwan Inspiration Association.
The association published results of its latest poll Wednesday, which found 82.3% of respondents viewed the threats as serious, including 47.7% who considered them “very serious,” per Newtalk. Also, 17.6% found the threats not serious.
The concern cut across party lines, with 95% of DPP supporters, 69% of KMT supporters and 71% of TPP supporters saying the activities posed a serious threat.
Chiu Shi-yi (邱師儀), a political science professor at Tunghai University, said the results reflected a “consensus” in Taiwan over how to view China and the CCP.
The poll also found that 68.8% of respondents supported increasing defense spending, including 39.4% who strongly supported it. Taiwan’s Cabinet in August proposed a record NT$1.12 trillion (US$35.15 billion) defense budget for 2027.
According to the poll, 67.3% said an increased military presence by the US and other democracies in the Taiwan Strait would help security, with 28.3% saying it would help “very much.”
Fan Shih-ping (范世平), an East Asian studies professor at National Taiwan Normal University, said that despite political divisions, public opinion remained broadly supportive of national security and opposition to CCP infiltration.
The poll surveyed people aged 20 and above nationwide and collected 1,201 valid responses between Sept. 10-15.

06:48:25 UTC
15:48:25 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taoyuan Mayor Chang San-cheng (張善政) is highlighting infrastructure, maternal health, and childcare policies as he seeks re-election.
Before running for Taoyuan mayor in 2022, Chang accumulated experience in academia, the private sector, and government, per Business Today. He became a professor at National Taiwan University at 33 and later became the first director-general of the National Center for High-performance Computing.
Chang worked for Acer for 10 years before joining Google. He later entered the central government at the invitation of former President Ma Ying-jeou (馬英九), serving as minister without portfolio, minister of the now-defunct Ministry of Science and Technology, vice premier, and premier during the final months of Ma’s presidency.
Reflecting on his tenure as premier, Chang attributed his favorable polling numbers in part to what he described as reduced criticism from the DPP after it won the 2016 presidential election.
Chang has argued that his academic training allows him to apply technical knowledge to city governance, taking what he describes as a practical approach to municipal problems, per CNews.
Chang also cited his experience responding to the 2016 Tainan earthquake, when he worked with then-Tainan Mayor Lai Ching-te (賴清德), as providing important experience in disaster management and emergency response. Since becoming mayor, Chang said he continued to use smart technology to improve government efficiency, per Business Today.
Chang argued that while major transportation improvements require substantial investment and time, smaller measures can also produce noticeable results. He cited the use of artificial intelligence-controlled traffic lights and offset left-turn lanes as examples, per Business Today.
Taoyuan City Government also introduced smaller buses that can be driven with a standard passenger car license and increased base pay for bus drivers in training. Chang said these measures were intended to address a driver shortage that had contributed to problems with Taoyuan’s bus services.
Alongside these lower-cost measures, Chang pursued longer-term projects, including new MRT lines, development of Taoyuan Aerotropolis around the airport, expansion of Longtan Science Park, and the establishment of a Department of Women and Children Development. He also introduced policies aimed at supporting families, including increased pay for substitute teachers and the establishment of the Public Health Center for Women and Children to provide specialized care focused on early childhood development, per China Times.
Looking ahead, Chang has identified traffic, the urban-rural divide, and the slow pace of urban renewal as areas requiring further improvement, per UDN. He said his administration spent time addressing issues inherited from his predecessor and called on the central government, led by the DPP, to support key policies, including plans to move Taoyuan’s railway lines underground, per UDN.
Responding to criticism that he is not sufficiently hands-on, Chang said the social demands of being mayor initially caught him off guard, per Commercial Times. He said he eventually came to enjoy interacting with constituents after seeing their positive responses.
Chang added that as residents became more accustomed to his approach of working from the office to deliver tangible benefits, his relatively lower public visibility became less of an issue over time.

Russia delivers upgraded Su-57 stealth fighters to its air force
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
06:39:04 UTC
15:39:04 KST

- Russia's United Aircraft Corporation delivered a new batch of Su-57 fighter jets to the Russian Aerospace Forces in an upgraded "new technical configuration."
- Rostec did not disclose the number of aircraft delivered, and Russia has built more than 44 Su-57s as of 2026, including test aircraft.
Russia has delivered a new batch of Su-57 stealth fighters to its air force, and the jets come in what the manufacturer calls a “new technical configuration,” with upgraded onboard systems and an expanded set of weapons options. Rostec, the state conglomerate that owns manufacturer United Aircraft Corporation, announced the delivery but did not say how many aircraft were included or specify which systems were changed.
Each aircraft went through a full cycle of factory testing before military pilots evaluated it across a range of operating conditions. Only after clearing those checks did the jets fly to their home airbase.
Rostec used nearly identical language, “new technical configuration,” to describe an earlier batch of Su-57s delivered in February. That batch reportedly included a new heads-up display for the pilot, a revised arrangement of formation lights, and additional infrared sensors feeding into the aircraft’s targeting system. Rostec’s statement does not make clear whether this delivery represents a further upgrade beyond February’s batch or more aircraft built to that same standard.
“To fulfill the targets set by the Russian Defense Ministry for the supply of highly sought-after weapons and military equipment to the troops, crews of the Russian Aerospace Forces have accepted the Su-57 aircraft in their new technical configuration,” a Su-57 pilot said in Rostec’s statement. “The aircraft has already shown itself well during the special military operation, and the new technical configuration will help expand the range of tasks for which this type of aircraft is used. The promising capabilities built into the aviation weapons complex make it possible to employ new types of airborne weapons.”
“The fifth-generation Su-57 aviation complex is the best aircraft in its class,” said Vadim Badeha, general director of United Aircraft Corporation. “Unconditional fulfillment of the state defense order for the supply of these and other tactical aviation aircraft is our top priority. Our specialists, in cooperation with other Rostec companies, are constantly improving production processes to ensure the necessary pace of aircraft manufacturing.”
The Su-57 is Russia’s fifth-generation stealth fighter, built to strike targets in the air, on the ground, and at sea. Its airframe and coatings are designed to reduce its radar signature, and Russia says it can operate around the clock, including in bad weather or when an adversary is jamming its sensors. The aircraft first flew in 2010 and formally entered Russian service in 2020. Rostec says more than 44 have been built as of 2026, a figure that includes early test aircraft alongside combat-ready jets.
United Aircraft Corporation has also test-flown the Su-57 with a new engine, the Izdeliye 177, which Rostec says produces up to 16,000 kg (35,000 pounds) of thrust with the afterburner engaged. That engine is a step toward a further upgraded variant, the Su-57M, which is expected to use an even more powerful engine, the Izdeliye 30.

US-seized tankers of Iranian oil are in Atlantic: tracker
Three Iran-linked oil tankers seized by the United States and carrying nearly six million barrels of Iranian crude oil were in the Atlantic Ocean on Thursday, tracking data indicated.
They did not have their destination marked on their transponders, but specialist website TankerTrackers said Wednesday on X that they were heading towards the United States.
"Nearly six million barrels (valued at nearly $600 million) of seized Iranian crude oil are quietly crossing the Atlantic Ocean towards the United States of America," the post said.
One of the tankers, the Majestic X, briefly listed the US as its destination from July 31 to August 2, as it began heading towards the Atlantic from waters off Malaysia, according to tracking data from maritime platform Kpler.
The three tankers are sanctioned by the United States under programmes aimed at limiting Iran's oil exports.
They were seized after the US started a blockade of Iranian ports in retaliation for Iran's closing of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for oil exports from Gulf countries.

They also raised their prediction for 2027 slightly to 1.1 percent.
"The German economy performed significantly better in the first half of 2026 than had been expected in spring," they said, with growth supported by strong exports and a robust manufacturing sector.
"Although the energy price shock associated with the Iran war has weighed on the German economy, the higher prices for motor fuels and heating oil have so far had little spillover effect on broader consumer prices," they added.
Business rivals in the Gulf region had suffered "significant production disruptions" due to the US war on Iran, they noted.
And German manufacturers have been benefitting from business being redirected to them from harder-hit parts of the global economy.
"The need for fiscal consolidation is growing," the institutes said.
The forecasts are compiled by the DIW, RWI, Ifo, IWH and IfW institutes.

Top Ukrainian, Iranian diplomats discuss mutual steps to prevent further tensions
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
06:37:54 UTC
15:37:54 KST

Burc Eruygur
24 September 2026•Update: 24 September 2026
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said he and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held talks Wednesday on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, focusing on mutual steps to prevent further bilateral tensions.
In a statement on US social media company X, Sybiha said the talks followed up on their most recent phone call in July, after which he said Kyiv sought to avoid "unnecessary escalation" with Tehran amid its accusation against Ukraine of attacking an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea.
“Diplomacy is about direct conversation, even in challenging circumstances,” Sybiha said, noting that their conversation in New York focused on “mutual steps to prevent further aggravation of tensions between our countries.”
He stressed that they agreed to keep existing communication channels open and also exchanged views on the situation in the Middle East and Europe, as well as various tracks of ongoing peace efforts.
“I reiterated Ukraine's position in support of a sooner restoration of peace and stability in both our regions,” he added.
In July, Sybiha and Araghchi held a phone call days after Tehran accused Kyiv of attacking an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea, killing one sailor and injuring another.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces had struck vessels involved in military cargo shipments linked to Iran without identifying any specific ship.
At the time, Sybiha noted that he held a "frank" conversation with his Iranian counterpart, adding that he stressed that Ukraine’s goal is to avoid “unnecessary escalation” with Iran and that his country’s actions are aimed “solely at defending our country from Russian aggression” and never intended to target civilian vessels or people.
"It is Russia who bears full responsibility for all provocations and casualties," he said, adding that he emphasized the need to refrain from escalatory steps and to "end any support for Russia's war against Ukraine."
Araghchi, for his part, said his Ukrainian counterpart assured him that the incident was unintentional and Kyiv sought no escalation.
"Iran does not seek escalation either, but made clear any attack on our citizens or interests is unacceptable. There must be restitution for losses," Araghchi added.

Pezeshkian reiterates Iran's will to resist pressure
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
06:35:10 UTC
15:35:10 KST

President Pezeshkian and his Swiss counterpart Guy Parmelin discussed recent regional and international developments and the need to strengthen diplomatic mechanisms to reduce tensions during a meeting on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York.
The Iranian president outlined Tehran’s position on recent developments and stressed the importance of respecting fundamental principles of international law. He also expressed Iran’s readiness to expand relations and cooperation with countries on the basis of mutual respect.
During the meeting, President Pezeshkian said the recent US and Israeli acts of aggression against Iran, including attacks on the country’s infrastructure and civilian facilities and the targeting of the Leader, officials, commanders, scientists and citizens, were contrary to fundamental principles of international law, humanitarian standards and obligations arising from international documents and treaties.
He stressed the need for all parties to respect national sovereignty and territorial integrity, the prohibition of the use of force, and the settlement of disputes through dialogue and peaceful mechanisms.
The Iranian president said Tehran was prepared to expand its relations and cooperation with all countries based on mutual respect, common interests, good-neighborly relations, sovereign equality and accepted international principles and rules.
President Pezeshkian also said Iran would respond to pressure, threats and policies based on force while defending its national rights and interests. He stressed that disputes could be resolved only through dialogue, diplomacy and compliance with international commitments, adding that lasting stability and security could not be established through coercive and unilateral measures.
The Iranian president presented his Swiss counterpart with a copy of In the Name of HELP, a book containing the names and photographs of Iranians killed in the recent war. The book was intended to recall false claims of assistance by the United States and its allies.
President Parmelin, for his part, referred to the longstanding relations and good ties between Iran and Switzerland and stressed the importance of maintaining dialogue and using diplomatic channels to manage regional crises.
The Swiss president recalled Switzerland’s role in previous diplomatic efforts and initiatives, as well as its history of representing US interests in Iran. He described relations between Tehran and Bern as important and longstanding.
President Parmelin also expressed concern over the situation in the region and said Switzerland was prepared to use its diplomatic capacity to help reduce tensions, facilitate dialogue and create conditions for moving beyond the current situation.
He stressed the need to end the cycle of tensions and conflict and to pursue political and diplomatic solutions aimed at restoring stability and preventing further escalation.

General Staff: Russia has lost 1,523,980 troops in Ukraine since Feb. 24, 2022
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
06:31:21 UTC
15:31:21 KST

Russia has lost around 1,523,980 troops in Ukraine since the beginning of its full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported on Sept. 24.
The number includes 1,540 casualties that Russian forces suffered over the past day.
According to the report, Russia has also lost 12,367 tanks, 25,402 armored combat vehicles, 152,782 vehicles and fuel tanks, 50,240 artillery systems, 2,154 multiple launch rocket systems, 1,669 air defense systems, 443 aircraft, 356 helicopters, 2,727 unmanned ground vehicles, 35 ships and boats, and two submarines.
Ukraine's General Staff has not revealed its own losses during the full-scale invasion, citing operational secrecy.
Independent Western think-tank reports agree that the Russian casualties significantly surpass Ukraine's losses, with the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimating the ratio to be "roughly 2.5:1 or 2:1."
A January 2026 CSIS report said Ukraine has likely suffered between 500,000 and 600,000 casualties from February 2022 to December 2025, of which between 100,000 and 140,000 are thought to be killed in action (KIA).
While Ukrainian officials rarely disclose the figure, President Volodymyr Zelensky told France TV on Feb. 4 that at least 55,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed in action since the beginning of the full-scale war, in addition to a lot more missing in action (MIAs).
The intensity of Russian drone attacks and the fighting has made it extremely difficult for Ukraine to retrieve the bodies of fallen soldiers, which are needed for DNA confirmation.

Visa restrictions leave thousands of Turkish truck drivers stranded at EU borders
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
06:31:16 UTC
15:31:16 KST

(AA Photo)
Turkish truck drivers transporting goods between Türkiye and the European Union have increasingly been turned back at border crossings in recent months due to the Schengen area’s 90/180-day rule, creating disruptions for road freight transport and trade flows.
The issue affects a significant share of Türkiye’s exports to the EU, nearly half of which are transported by road. Reports of drivers being denied entry at border checkpoints, including Italy’s Trieste and the Kapıkule crossing on the Bulgarian border, have raised concerns among transport operators and exporters.
Some $111 billion worth of goods were transported by road to the European Union in 2025.
According to Şerafettin Aras, president of the International Transporters Association (UND), around 25,000 of Türkiye’s 50,000 international truck drivers have been affected by the restrictions.
Under Schengen rules, visa holders may spend no more than 90 days within any rolling 180-day period in the bloc. Aras said commercial drivers inevitably reach that limit because of time spent loading and unloading cargo as well as waiting at border crossings.
Aras said the problem extends beyond the transport sector, noting that nearly half of Türkiye’s exports are destined for EU countries and that 42 percent of those shipments travel by road.
“Fifty percent of exporting companies producing in Türkiye are European-owned firms. We transport their products. Turkish drivers also provide transport services to destinations where EU trucks do not operate. This is not only a problem for Türkiye but also a situation that negatively affects the foreign trade of EU countries,” he said.
Aras said inspections related to the rule had intensified at border crossings over the past two months, forcing changes in transport routes. He added that the restrictions were affecting not only trade between Türkiye and the EU but also freight movements from Europe to third countries.
“Now there are substantial shipments from the EU to Syria, Saudi Arabia and Dubai. Turkish transport companies carry out these operations. However, because of the Schengen rule, this trade cannot be conducted as it should be,” he said.
While transport contracts contain penalty clauses for delivery delays, Aras said the current situation is being treated as a force majeure event.
“There are order cancellations at the moment. It is possible that cancellations will increase in the coming days. Official discussions on the issue are continuing. For a solution, commercial vehicle drivers should not be treated under the same framework as tourists. A D-type visa is necessary,” he said.
A D-type national visa allows foreign nationals to stay in a country for more than 90 days for purposes such as work, education or family reunification.

Fondation Beyeler Expands with Three New Buildings by Peter Zumthor
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
06:30:00 UTC
15:30:00 KST

The Fondation Beyeler in Riehen, Switzerland, is expanding its museum ensemble with three new buildings by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor, an enlarged and restored park, and the adaptive reuse of several historic structures. The expansion extends the existing museum designed by Renzo Piano, adding exhibition, education, cultural, and public spaces while opening a previously private section of the surrounding landscape to visitors. The expanded ensemble will begin welcoming visitors on September 26, 2026, during a preview phase running through January 14, 2027, before fully opening on January 15. Zumthor's additions comprise the Wyss Museum, the Ammann Pavilion, and the Erlen Torhaus, positioned within the existing landscape and differentiated through their programmes, forms, and material treatments.
The largest addition, the three-storey Wyss Museum, adds approximately 1,500 square meters of exhibition space. Its Y-shaped plan is arranged around existing trees, including a ginkgo, a redwood, and a group of plane trees, while large windows frame views toward the surrounding landscape, including the Black Forest and Jura region. An upper-level terrace connects the building to the park via an external staircase. Locally quarried Jura limestone is used throughout the building, including in the rammed-concrete façade, terrazzo flooring, staircases, benches, and wall finishes. The new museum will accommodate works from the Fondation Beyeler collection alongside loans from private collections and will also host temporary exhibition projects.
Located between the two museum buildings and the historic structures, the Ammann Pavilion acts as a public gathering space. Its single-storey glass and oak structure opens directly onto the park, with floor-to-ceiling glazing providing views across the landscape. The pavilion will function as a freely accessible public lounge during the day and accommodate concerts, performances, talks, film screenings, and other cultural events in the evening. At the edge of the site, the Erlen Torhaus forms a transition between the urban fabric and the adjacent nature reserve. Its timber-frame structure contains artwork handling facilities and workspaces, with a stained oak façade referencing Zumthor's studio in Haldenstein.
Landscape forms an integral part of the expansion, with the addition of almost 10,000 square meters of formerly private parkland nearly doubling the size of Beyeler Park. Both sections of the park were originally laid out in the 19th century as English landscape gardens by Jean-François Caillat. The expanded area retains mature trees and water lily ponds while introducing species-rich meadows, wooded areas, grasses, perennials, and native orchids. A bridge designed by Zumthor crosses the pond, while the park connects directly to the Landschaftspark Wiese nature reserve. Existing works by Alexander Calder, Jenny Holzer, Ellsworth Kelly, Philippe Parreno, Thomas Schütte, and Fischli/Weiss will be joined by new works by Louise Bourgeois, Pierre Huyghe, Rachel Whiteread, and Fujiko Nakaya.
The project also incorporates several restored historic buildings, adapting them for art education, music, botany, and experimental projects. The heritage-listed Orangerie, redesigned by India Mahdavi, combines a small greenhouse with a plant-focused shop, while the Ammann Atelier provides space for workshops and educational programmes. The Salon introduces a listening lounge with a collection of more than 2,000 vinyl records, and the compact Folly provides an experimental exhibition space for artists.
The expanded ensemble will be introduced through a year-long cultural programme beginning in autumn 2026. The inaugural exhibition, "Constellations," will bring together more than 200 works from the Fondation Beyeler collection and private collections across the two museum buildings, the expanded park, and the historic structures. Running from September 26, 2026, to September 5, 2027, the exhibition will evolve with the seasons, establishing changing relationships between art, architecture, and landscape.
In other recent opening news, the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles, designed by MAD Architects with landscape architecture by Studio-MLA and Stantec as executive architect; Mecanoo's Lawson Centre for Sustainability at Trinity College in Toronto, developed with RDHA as a sustainable academic and residential "living lab"; and the African Futures Institute's new headquarters in Accra, which adapts a former tile warehouse in Osu into a centre for architectural education, research, exhibitions, and public programmes.

Chinese drug Loberamisal extends stroke treatment window from 6 hours to 2 days
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
06:29:27 UTC
15:29:27 KST

Chinese drug loberamisal extends stroke treatment window from 6 hours to 2 days
Large-scale clinical trial with nearly 1,000 patients from 32 hospitals delivers 13 per cent leap in recovery over standard care alone
Brain cells start dying within minutes of a clot blocking an artery, leading to facial droop, affected speech and in severe cases, paralysis or death. Emergency treatments, such as clot-busting drugs or surgery, must be given within a maximum of six hours.
According to a study published by the top-tier Journal of the American Medical Association on September 10, clinical trials of the drug loberamisal found it was possible to expand the time available to 48 hours.
The large-scale multicentre phase 3 trial found that 70 per cent of patients who received loberamisal intravenously within two days of a stroke regained complete functional independence – an increase of 13 percentage points over standard care alone.

The AFP news agency, quoting two diplomatic sources, also reported that Washington refused to issue the visa. One source called the move a “clear violation of the UN’s agreement with the US” while another said the visa had been “conditioned” on al-Burhan accepting the three-month truce.
‘Political pressure’
Sudan’s UN ambassador, Al-Harith Idriss Al-Harith, wrote to Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to request the UN’s “immediate intervention” with US authorities, according to Reuters.
Stephane Dujarric, a spokesman for Guterres, said the UN chief was “deeply concerned” that the visa had reportedly not been issued. He told the AFP that the UN Secretariat has urged the US, as host country, to ensure visas were issued in accordance with its obligations under the UN Headquarters Agreement and in time for al-Burhan to participate in the General Assembly.
Sudanese activist Mamoun al-Sheikh denounced the US move in a post on Facebook, saying: “Even if the visa is withheld, it will not silence Sudan’s voice.”
Another activist, Sayed Al-Mazaj, described linking the visa to a proposed 90-day ceasefire as “a tool for political pressure”. And in a video posted on X, Sudanese journalist Diaa Al-Din Bilal said barring al-Burhan from New York would not force him to accept the US position and could instead boost his popularity and rally support around him.
Another X user, @Atifazhri, also denounced the US move, noting that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court on charges of war crimes in Gaza, had been granted a visa.
“The issue is double standards – when visas become instruments of political coercion against a sovereign state while far more serious cases are treated differently. International law and justice cannot be applied selectively,” the user wrote.
US questions al-Burhan’s legitimacy
The State Department issued a statement on Tuesday that did not directly address al-Burhan’s visa but called into question his legitimacy. Its spokesman Tommy Pigott said neither the Sudanese army nor the RSF “nor their respective leaders, represent legitimate, constitutional governance for Sudan”.
He added the US would “seek to raise the cost of continued conflict on all belligerents”.
Sudan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs hit back on Wednesday, calling on the US to engage positively with the country’s government. Any peace initiative, it said, must “be grounded in respect for Sudan’s sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity, and legitimate national institutions”.
“It must also address the root causes of the war’s continuation — foremost among them, negative foreign interference,” the ministry added.
Al-Burhan has been Sudan’s de facto leader since 2019 although the African Union and Western powers withdrew recognition after a 2021 coup that he led with Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, the RSF’s leader, against the civilian leadership.
He has rejected externally imposed ceasefires, arguing that earlier pauses in the fighting benefitted the paramilitary group.
The US has also refused visas to Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas and some members of Iran’s delegation to the UN.

Zelenskyy denies reports of tense talks with von der Leyen: meeting was "absolutely positive"
