China Focus: Young Chinese find roots, inspiration in Long March legacy
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
11:52:20 CST
12:52:20 KST

Artists stage a Red Army-themed performance in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, June 9, 2026. (Xinhua/Xu Hongyan)
GUIYANG, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- On stage, Red Army soldiers on the Long March braved raging rivers, snow-covered mountains and vast grasslands. Some fell amid a hail of gunfire, while others marched on to the end.
When the performance ended and the lights came up, 24-year-old actor Tian Hongqiang found himself back in the present, witnessing a new China for all those who had sacrificed their lives.
"I saw a glimmer of light shining in the audience's eyes. Grey-haired elders and young students in school uniforms gave us their thumbs-up," Tian said. "That makes me feel the power of the spirit we are trying to convey."
For over two years, Tian has performed in "The Great Turning Point," a large-scale immersive production about the Long March being staged in Zunyi, southwest China's Guizhou Province.
Known as China's "city of historic turning point," Zunyi holds a special place in the nation's history. In January 1935, during the Long March, the Communist Party of China (CPC) convened the Zunyi Meeting in a two-story building here at a critical historical crossroads.
In October 1934, the CPC was forced to retreat from the Central Soviet Area in east China's Jiangxi and move northwest after enduring a series of encirclement campaigns by rival forces of the Kuomintang party (KMT). The setback was the result of left-leaning errors in military strategy and rigid Soviet-inspired dogmatism.
The CPC-led Red Army fought its way across the Xiangjiang River in Guangxi and broke through the KMT troops' blockade, but suffered tens of thousands of casualties in the battle.
The three-day meeting was thus convened to draw lessons. In the end, many key issues were resolved, including the establishment of a new Party leadership with Mao Zedong at the helm.
Today, Zunyi is one of China's best-known destinations for historical education tours, which take visitors to sites associated with the country's revolutionary history.
This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. In Zunyi, the history that once unfolded in meeting rooms, mountain passes and battlefields is being retold via theater, immersive experiences and cultural products, drawing younger generations closer to the historical events.
"The Great Turning Point," centered on the history of the Zunyi Meeting, premiered on Jan. 15, 2024, the meeting's 89th anniversary, and has staged more than 2,500 performances so far.
Wang Liming, a marketing executive with the company behind the production, said about 60 percent of its audience are 25 to 50 years old, with many parents joining their children to watch.
"We hope to help young people develop an emotional connection with this history, so that it is no longer just words and pictures in a textbook," Wang said.
Among the audience was 10-year-old Xu Chen'en, who traveled from Chongqing Municipality in southwest China with her mother, Chen Jinghong.
"I think the Red Army soldiers were very brave," Xu said. "We should learn from them and face our own difficulties courageously."
Her mother sees the experience as a form of education that sinks in over time. "It is like planting a seed in her heart," Chen said. "She can experience the culture of the Long March now and gradually come to understand it as she grows up."
For another visitor, surnamed Xia, the performance became an experience shared by three generations. She watched it with her 56-year-old aunt and 85-year-old grandmother.
"My grandmother's generation has a strong emotional bond with this history, and she was deeply moved," Xia said. "For us, theater makes it much more immersive."
The family's next stop was Loushan Pass, north of Zunyi, another landmark on the Long March route.
After the Zunyi Meeting, the Red Army achieved a major victory there. What was once a battlefield is now a popular tourism destination.
Twice a day, a live-action performance lasting nearly an hour recreates battle scenes. Roughly 90 performers are residents of nearby villages.
"We want to make the spirit of the Long March something visitors can see and experience," said Zhu Jingbo, a local culture and tourism official.
Visitors can take part in the performance, playing roles as local residents, helping to transport supplies and tending to wounded soldiers. Zhu said creators consulted historians while developing the show, including firsthand accounts of locals guiding Red Army troops across the region.
This approach, he said, is intended to move beyond static museum displays, make revolutionary history more accessible to younger visitors, and create new opportunities for local communities.
Around 15,000 students visit the Loushan Pass area each year on educational trips. Villagers who take part in performances can earn an additional 2,000 to 3,000 yuan (approximately 298 to 447 U.S. dollars) a month, depending on their roles.
Such immersive experiences are part of a wider shift in China's revolutionary education tours. In recent years, historical education tours have increasingly diversified, with performances, study tours and cultural products complementing traditional visits to memorials and historic sites.
China's plan for building the country into a tourism powerhouse during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) also calls for further exploring the historical and contemporary value of revolutionary heritage, improving exhibitions at revolutionary tourism sites, and expanding cultural products and performances.
Thus the creative reinterpretation of the Long March spirit stretches far beyond museums and scenic spots. Zunyi's bustling downtown Red Army Street boasts a full range of Long March-themed cultural products, including figurines, backpacks and custom cups, making revolutionary culture accessible to younger audiences.
Near the historical site of the Zunyi Meeting, designer Han Bing sells small Red Army figurines. He said many of his customers are students, particularly from primary and middle schools, while older visitors often buy the figurines as gifts for children.
The shop, which opened in 2019, has maintained brisk business, with daily sales sometimes exceeding 12,000 yuan.
For Han, the connection with the Long March is personal.
He comes from Liping County in Guizhou, the first county seat reached by the Central Red Army after entering the province.
Han grew up hearing a family story about a wooden bridge across the Bazhou River that Red Army troops once crossed. His great-grandfather, he said, helped build the bridge, which later became known locally as the "Red Army Bridge."
Influenced by his family, Han developed an interest in revolutionary history at an early age and later studied art.
Growing up during the early decades of China's reform and opening-up, he said he was initially fascinated by cultures from abroad. But when he started his own business and began exploring Chinese history and revolutionary culture more deeply, he felt as though he had found his roots.
"I wanted to share that feeling with other people," Han said. "So I turned images of Red Army soldiers into figurines, using a form that younger people can relate to."
When asked why the Long March should still be remembered 90 years later, he answered with a story from his own life.
At the most difficult point in his entrepreneurial journey, Han said he had lost nearly all the money he had invested. Alone, he went to the top of Loushan Pass and recited a poem written there by Mao Zedong. "Fear not the strong pass iron-clad on all sides! The summit's now surmounted with big strides..."
As he recited, he said his determination gradually returned.
"What inspires me most is the enduring optimism of the Long March, the sense that hope never dies," Han said. "It's an inexhaustible source of strength." ■
This photo taken on Aug. 17, 2026 shows a view of Loushan Pass in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province. (Xinhua/Shi Qiangui)

The Tuesday fill-up myth — and how to find the cheapest fuel in your city
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
03:46:24 UTC
12:46:24 KST

IN BRIEF:
- Fuel prices are increasing amid rising tensions in the Middle East.
- The government reports real-time petrol prices, but some apps make them easier to track.
Australians are paying more at the bowser than they have in months, amid strikes in the Middle East leading to oil price shocks and the fuel excise being paid in full.
A cut to the fuel excise, implemented in April to offer Australians relief amid skyrocketing petrol prices at the height of tensions in the war in the Middle East, ended on 3 August.
Opening the war in the Middle East to a new front, Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen seized control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and disabled the vital Saudi Arabian East-West pipeline, causing oil price spikes.
Brent crude shot above US$100 ($142) on Monday, more than 8 cents per litre, according to the NRMA weekly fuel report. The report also predicted that wholesale prices would continue to rise and that average unleaded prices would rise in Sydney from 237.8 cents per litre to at least 240 cents per litre over the coming week.
Diesel prices similarly spiked with Sydney’s current average diesel price at 286.1 cents per litre.
News that makes sense
Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.
Experts have warned that these fluctuations could become the "new normal".
Alison Reeve, program director of energy and climate at the Grattan Institute, told SBS News this week that while Australians can "adjust to a new normal" of sustained high fuel costs, it's "volatility that's actually more dangerous to the economy than a price that goes high and stays high".
Fluctuating prices make it more challenging for governments, industry, and households to plan ahead.
However, there are a range of simple hacks you can use to find more affordable fuel amid the uncertainty.
Where to find the cheapest fuel in your city
Peter Khoury, head of media at the NRMA, said price gaps between petrol stations can be significant — sometimes as much as 20 or 30 cents per litre — in the same neighbourhood.
"We know that there are several service stations now charging over $3 a day for a litre of diesel, whereas the average is still below $3 and $2.94. So we want people to find the best bargain before they fill up."
But thankfully, he said, "it's easier to do that now than it has ever been before".
In Australia, each state and territory government receives and publishes real-time data on petrol prices. These are available to all motorists through state government websites and some apps.
Additionally, for some states, free apps integrate this public government data with GPS integration to direct you to your closest and cheapest station, or the ability to compare prices across areas.
Others, such as Petrol Spy and Fuel Map, use a mix of crowdsourced and government data, depending on where you are in Australia.
Petrol Spy (nationwide)
Petrol Spy AU/NZ is a free app that covers almost 8,500 petrol stations across Australia. It uses government data on prices for all states and territories except for Victoria, where it employs crowdsourced updates. Petrol Spy also tracks historical pricing trends and graphs to show whether fuel prices are rising or falling in major metropolitan areas.
Fuel Map (nationwide)
The app and website use crowd-sourced data from across Australia and government data for WA, NSW and Queensland.
My NRMA (Members only, NSW/ACT)
My NRMA is the membership, rewards, and lifestyle program offered by the National Roads and Motorists' Association in Australia. Its FuelFinder app allows consumers to compare fuel prices nearby, set alerts when prices drop and stack fuel discounts to save.
MotorMouth (nationwide)
One of the free fuel price comparison apps that is recommended by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.
Vroom Fuel Price Compare (QLD, NSW, TAS, and WA)
An app that uses official state government pricing databases to show up-to-date fuel costs.
The government resources include:
NSW/ACT
NSW Fuel Check (website and app)
Northern Territory
MyFuel NT (website)
Tasmania
FuelCheck TAS (website and app)
South Australia
RAA SA (website and app)
Victoria
ServoSaver via the Service Victoria app
Western Australia
WA FuelWatch (website and app)
Which day is best to fill up?
The short answer is there isn't one, despite a persistent myth that Tuesday is the optimal day.
Khoury said Perth was the only Australian city still on a seven-day petrol price cycle.
"It might still be that Tuesday is the cheapest day in Perth and then Wednesday is the most expensive as it's a seven-day cycle, but apart from there, there's no particular day. "
"It really is a matter of just making sure you check those prices before you fill up."
Khoury's message was clear: the best way to save money at the bowser was a little bit of planning.
"Plot your journey," he said.
"There's always going to be a spread of prices, no matter where you live, but also, if you're heading away for the holidays, there is every chance you're going to drive to or through a place that's cheaper than where you are.
"Find the cheaper servos and the cheapest towns, because you can save a lot of money."

Two Iranian officials to face trial in absentia over 1994 attack on Argentinian Jewish center
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
03:44:04 UTC
12:44:04 KST

Two senior officials at the heart of Iran’s military and national security establishment are among the eight people set to face trial in absentia over their alleged roles in the 1994 terrorist bombing of the AMIA Jewish community center in Buenos Aires.
Argentine Federal Judge Daniel Rafecas issued the 648-page ruling Monday, formally processing the suspects and ordering an asset freeze of up to $500 million for each. The ruling attributes different roles to the suspects, ranging from senior Iranian officials who allegedly made and facilitated the decision to carry out the attack to individuals accused of providing diplomatic and operational support.
Ahmad Vahidi, the current commander-in-chief of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, and Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, are among seven Iranian citizens and one Lebanese national formally charged in the case.
The other defendants are former Iranian intelligence minister Ali Fallahian; former foreign minister Ali Akbar Velayati; former Iranian diplomat Hadi Soleimanpour; former cultural attaché in Buenos Aires Mohsen Rabbani; former embassy official Ahmad Reza Asghari; and alleged Hezbollah operative Salman Raouf Salman, also known as Samuel Salman El Reda.
The judge charged the defendants with aggravated homicide and injuries motivated by racial or religious hatred. He classified the bombing as both a crime against humanity and an act of genocide.
Deadliest terrorist attack in Argentine history
The July 18, 1994 bombing of the AMIA building killed 85 people and injured over 300, remaining the deadliest terrorist attack in Argentine history.
The ruling was handed down after almost seven months of Iran’s war with the US and Israel, with the Islamic Republic’s nuclear program at the center of international debate.
Argentine President Javier Milei, known for his pro-Israel views, noted the prosecution in his remarks Wednesday at the annual United Nations General Assembly and placed it in the context of the threat he said Iran poses to the West.
“We have also made a geopolitical choice: We have aligned ourselves unequivocally with the West, with the United States and with Israel, countries with which we share a deep affinity of values and strategic complementarity,” he said. “That is why we condemn the Iranian regime’s attacks on the State of Israel, we have designated Iran’s Revolutionary Guard as a terrorist organization, and continue to seek justice for the two attacks carried out on Argentine soil in 1992 and 1994.”
The indictments followed a unanimous ruling also on Monday by the federal appeals court upholding the constitutionality of applying Argentina’s trial-in-absentia law to the AMIA case. The legislation, enacted in 2025, allows proceedings involving terrorism and crimes against humanity to continue when defendants deliberately evade Argentine justice.
The Jewish umbrella organization DAIA welcomed the decision. “Thirty-two years after the bombing of the AMIA-DAIA building, Argentina’s courts have taken a major step in the pursuit of truth and justice,” it said in a post on X/Twitter. The post featured photos of the suspects formally charged by an Argentine judge under the headline “Historic Event.”
AMIA, in a statement posted Tuesday, said the decision marks “a decisive milestone in establishing the truth about the worst terrorist attack suffered by our country.” The trial date has not yet been set, but experts quoted by Argentine media estimate that it will take place next year. It would be the first trial in absentia in Argentina’s history.

He noted that Russia is destabilizing the situation in Europe through open aggression, hybrid operations, acts of sabotage and subversion.
"It displays the same imperial arrogance that in the past led to unimaginable suffering and the tragedies of two world wars," Nawrocki emphasized.
He added that it was not yet too late to "to restore the primacy of international law and strengthen the foundations of a system in which principles matter."
The Polish president also said that Russia, "guided by an imperial and neocolonial vision of the world," is trying to impose its will on others and questions the right of every nation to determine its own destiny.
Nawrocki emphasized that Poland is particularly aware of the consequences of Russian colonialism and imperialism.
"As a representative of a country neighboring Russia, I want to make it clear: we are not the ones seeking confrontation. We are strengthening our alliances, developing our military, and modernizing its equipment—not to wage war, but to prevent it," the Polish president stressed.
He underscored that Poland consistently regards NATO as the guarantor of Europe's security.
Nawrocki drew attention to the scale of Russia's hybrid war against Europe, which, he said, includes acts of sabotage, cyberattacks and destabilization operations, including an artificially created migration crisis.
"We are not dealing with isolated incidents, but with a sustained, well-thought-out strategy," the Polish leader said, stressing that the response to these actions must be "firm, consistent and united."
During his speech, Nawrocki also said that Poland seeks permanent participation in the work of the G20 and could represent Central Europe in that format.
"Poland wants to be the voice of this region—as a country that understands both the challenges of development and the importance of stable rules of the game in the international economy," he said.
As Ukrinform reported, the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency warned Poland about a possible Russian provocation targeting underwater telecommunications infrastructure, including cables in the Baltic Sea.

Former prosecutor general Kravchenko appears to have violated Vienna residency registration rules – UP

Former prosecutor general Kravchenko appears to have violated Vienna residency registration rules – UP
Former Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko appears to have violated the rules concerning his registered place of residence after moving to Vienna.
Source: an article by Ukrainska Pravda journalist Mykhailo Tkach
Details: The address listed in a document from the Austrian register is not Kravchenko's place of residence, as required by law.
Apartment No. 12 in the building at 7 Jordangasse is not a residential property but the office of CS Corporate Services GmbH. On its website, the company offers four services: domiciliation, meaning a registered legal address for Austrian limited liability companies; secretarial services; management services; and the sale of shelf companies that are already registered and ready to be transferred to a new owner.
The description of its domiciliation service says that an address in Vienna's first district, a few minutes' walk from the central square Stephansplatz, is registered with the Commercial Court, tax authorities and municipal authorities, while staff receive clients' post and, on their instructions, forward it unopened, scan it or reply to it themselves.
At least two dozen other legal entities are registered at the same address. They include subsidiaries of genuine international companies such as Duracell Austria GmbH and KPLER GmbH, but most are little-known companies, including Numitor, Febania, Nobeka, Furninet, Code Panda IT Solutions and others.
Kravchenko and his wife may have taken this step to conceal their actual place of residence in Vienna.
Registration in Vienna may also indicate that Kravchenko plans to establish legal residence in the Austrian capital, as it is well known that Austria does not extradite people wanted by Ukraine.
Tkach noted that when speaking to an influential official about the fate of Ukrainian officials in Austria, he had heard a wry comment: "At this rate, Vienna will soon have an entire Ukrainian government-in-exile."
Apart from the prosecutor general, who appears to have registered in Vienna only recently, the city is already home to former constitutional court chairman Oleksandr Tupytskyi, former National Bank governor Kyrylo Shevchenko, former MP Andrii Kholodov and many other "former" officials who have largely become stranded in one of Europe's best cities for years, either because of the war or to avoid punishment.
"In a city where there are no air-raid warnings, ballistic missiles, notices of suspicion issued by the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU) and the Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAPO) or the need to pay bail. In a city that does not extradite people wanted by Ukraine. For now," Tkach added.
Previously: It was reported that Kravchenko had left Ukraine on the night of 13-14 September, travelling abroad in a luxury taxi rather than an official vehicle and crossing the border at the Shehyni-Medyka checkpoint.
It is also known that Kravchenko submitted a letter of resignation from the prosecution service. It was accepted, and Kravchenko was dismissed from the prosecution service on 21 September.
Background:
- On 7 September, Kravchenko resigned as prosecutor general amid an investigation by NABU and SAPO into the alleged "protection" of scam call centres.
- On 14 September, Kravchenko said he had signed a notice of suspicion against NABU director Semen Kryvonos and accused NABU and SAPO of seizing materials from criminal proceedings against employees of the anti-corruption agencies in the course of searches conducted as part of Operation Carthage.
- According to Ukrainska Pravda sources in law enforcement, Kravchenko left Ukraine in an official car on the night of 13-14 September.
- He said in a statement that he had left to go on an official trip. According to an order by the prosecutor general dated 13 September, a copy of which was seen by Ukrainska Pravda, Kravchenko left for Paris for five days "to take part in PACE hearings on Ukrainian children". However, he was not listed among the speakers on the event agenda.
- President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged the Verkhovna Rada (Ukrainian parliament) to back Kravchenko's dismissal as prosecutor general.
- On 14 September, Zelenskyy signed a decree suspending Kravchenko as prosecutor general. The Verkhovna Rada later voted in favour of his dismissal.
- As of 21 September, Kravchenko, whose official trip abroad ended on 18 September, had not returned to work.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — DPP Taoyuan mayoral candidate Huang Shih-chieh (黃世杰) is seeking to distinguish himself from Mayor Chang San-cheng (張善政) by portraying himself as a more responsive, hands-on leader.
Huang was born into a farming family in Taoyuan, per Storm Media. His father, former Taoyuan Irrigation Association Chair Huang Chih-te (黃金德), is the only other member of the family to enter politics.
Huang Chih-te is a prominent local figure who previously served as a county councilor and deputy speaker of the council, per Liberty Times. Huang Shih-chieh, however, has said he had little involvement in his father’s political career.
Before joining former Taoyuan Mayor Cheng Wen-tsan’s (鄭文燦) administration, Huang pursued postgraduate studies at National Taiwan University and Columbia University, briefly considering an academic career. After leaving the city government to run for the legislature, he said his goal was to use legislation to address issues from the grassroots level.
When the DPP lost all of its Taoyuan legislative seats in the 2024 election, President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) appointed Huang as deputy justice minister. Some observers interpreted Lai’s selection of Huang as an attempt to reconcile with his father over reforms introduced under former President Tsai Ing-wen (蔡英文) that changed the system for selecting Irrigation Association officials from elections to government appointments, per Big Media.
Irrigation associations had historically been regarded as an important mechanism for the KMT to build local political support, although the Taoyuan association was controlled by the DPP, per CMedia.
In seeking to challenge Chang, Huang has focused on what he describes as the mayor’s governing style, arguing that municipal leaders need to take a more hands-on approach, per Liberty Times. Huang has criticized Chang’s response to what he regards as shortcomings in the city government, including its handling of flooding in May 2023.
Huang has also argued that Chang’s governing approach has failed to adequately address problems facing Taoyuan, including congestion in urban centers. He has proposed improving transportation by upgrading existing bus networks and accelerating construction of the Taoyuan MRT, per Liberty Times.
Huang has proposed establishing a city-operated bus service to better coordinate with future MRT services, per Mirror Media. He has also said he would push for the construction of a second medical center in Taoyuan to promote a more even distribution of medical resources.
Child care is another focus of Huang’s platform. He has argued that later marriage and smaller family sizes have increased the need for government support for couples raising children, per Mirror Media. He proposed creating a comprehensive map integrating information on daycare facilities, allowing parents to identify available services while helping the government determine which areas require additional investment.
Citing his legal background and experience in Cheng’s administration, Huang has argued that he is well positioned to navigate government bureaucracy and deliver results more quickly to constituents. He has attributed Taoyuan’s traffic problems and administrative challenges to what he describes as the city government’s failure to keep pace with rapid population growth, per UDN.

US President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington on Wednesday for a three-day visit that will test relations between the superpowers as tensions simmer over trade, technology, Taiwan and Tehran.
Xi’s first trip to the US in nearly three years was not expected to deliver major breakthroughs, but Washington and Beijing could extend their 11-month trade truce.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said they had reached a deal on an extension as Trump greeted Xi personally at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland after the Chinese leader's arrival, underscoring the visit's importance.

The welcome marked the first time in 11 years that a US president has greeted a foreign leader at Joint Base Andrews, according to C-SPAN, which tracks presidential events. The last such reception was for Pope Francis in 2015 during Barack Obama's presidency.
Positive signals on trade could soothe markets
A trade deal, even a limited one, could soothe global markets shaken by a 2025 tariff war that led to triple-digit levies between the world’s two biggest economies. Bessent told Fox News' "Special Report" that the deal would extend the truce through January 10. It had been set to expire on November 10.
Deep differences remain. The two countries are at odds on issues including export controls on rare-earth minerals and computer chips, China’s ties with Iran and US support for Taiwan.
The meeting comes at a difficult moment for Trump, who faces falling approval numbers as public discontent with his war on Iran grows. Xi, while also facing challenges at home, arrives in a seemingly stronger position, with his country's trade engine roaring. Some Republicans regard Beijing as an existential threat and are wary of Trump's friendly outreach to China's ruling Communist Party.
People familiar with the plans said Xi was likely to forcefully raise Beijing's claim to Taiwan, a topic Washington would prefer to avoid, while Trump was likely to maintain firm US export controls despite Xi’s objections. It was unclear whether Beijing would help Trump break a stalemate in the conflict with Iran.
But talks set for Thursday could nonetheless yield deals to lower tariffs in specific sectors, cooperate on drug trafficking and expand military-to-military dialogue. Trump is expected to seek the release of some Americans and others detained in China, according to the people.
The two countries could also agree to talk more on AI, where they are in fierce competition despite growing dangers.
The leaders themselves may not feel they need to compromise, analysts said.
"The president very much believes that over time the US economy is going to grow, the US will get stronger," said Edgard Kagan, a former White House official now with Washington's Center for Strategic and International Studies. "I think when Xi Jinping sits down with Donald Trump, he very much believes the US is in hurtling decline, and that time is on China's side."
State dinner with AI chiefs
Additional fanfare during the trip is due to include a state dinner with tech luminaries, a White House military ceremony including jet flyovers, and a visit to the National Archives where the original Declaration of Independence and Constitution are housed.
The state dinner on Thursday is expected to bring together chiefs of companies important in both markets like Apple's Tim Cook, Nvidia's Jensen Huang, and OpenAI's Sam Altman.
Despite their deep disagreements, both countries pressed ahead with the summit, which, analysts said, seeks to project stability between the world’s biggest factory and its biggest consumer.
As in their prior two meetings since 2025, the leaders are planning a highly scripted public spectacle. Instead of a joint press conference or statement at the end, the countries are expected to issue dueling announcements highlighting what each side hopes to convey to a domestic audience.
For Trump, the trip caps a week of diplomacy that began with a two-day stay in New York for the United Nations General Assembly. Nearly seven months of war with Iran have spiked energy prices in the US, and the president's Republican Party faces tough prospects in November’s congressional elections.
Xi has overseen a surge in China's foreign trade but faces weak household spending and a property market downturn. Sweeping corruption and discipline crackdowns in the military have helped cement Xi’s power but also raised questions about the People's Liberation Army's readiness.
Another meeting between Trump and Xi is seen as likely this year, potentially at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China in November or the Group of 20 meetings in the US in December.

IDF failed to defend Paga Outpost during Oct. 7, opening door for terrorists to massacre at Be'eri
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
03:12:57 UTC
12:12:57 KST

The IDF failed in its mission to defend the Paga Outpost, officially known as Magen Be’eri, during the October 7 massacre and did not prevent the area from falling into enemy hands, the military’s probe, released on Thursday, found.
The probe found that the failures at Paga Outpost reflected the systemic failures in preparedness for the attack in terms of the operational readiness of combat positions, the infrastructure required for fighting, soldiers lacking key equipment, and more.
The Infantry Brigade Combat Team (IBCT) at the location was not adequately prepared for the mission. However, the operational reality faced by the soldiers was that individual heroism and noteworthy actions occurred at both the junior officer and soldier levels, in both the company sector and at the outpost.
In total, 22 soldiers, including officers, were murdered during the massacre at the Paga Outpost, with an additional 18 wounded in action. Furthermore, terrorists succeeded in taking two soldiers as hostages and dragged them to the Gaza Strip.
Main conclusions and investigations of the storming of Paga Outpost
The probe drew seven main conclusions from the investigation into the storming of the Paga Outpost, the IDF’s failure to defend it, and the terrorists’ success in infiltrating the nearby Kibbutz Be’eri.
Firstly, the battle at the Paga Outpost was part of a broader attack, in which hundreds of terrorists entered through a myriad of infiltration routes and succeeded in surprising the IDF soldiers stationed at the outpost.
This brings us to the second point. Up until the infiltration and subsequent massacre began, the soldiers primarily dealt with local disturbances near the perimeter border fence. This affected their preparation for such an attack, as well as the training and drills they undertook.
Notably, their training did not include a scenario of a simultaneous surprise attack across the Israel-Gaza border. This included no drills or scenarios to prepare for a raid on either the outpost or Kibbutz Be’eri, the main location the outpost is meant to defend.
Thirdly, when the massacre began, the IBCT was not sufficiently prepared to defend the outpost. This is despite the fact that Paga Outpost was designed and constructed as a combat outpost with all necessary infrastructure and components.
Fourthly, the terrorists’ infiltration, along with mitigating the sector’s force multipliers, including intelligence collection capabilities and defensive firepower, enabled terrorists to both penetrate Paga Outpost and infiltrate Kibbutz Be’eri.
Fifthly, the terrorist infiltrators attacked the sector’s intelligence collection capabilities and the tank platoon poised to aid the outpost in its defense of the area. Subsequently, the terrorists succeeded in destroying a significant portion of the sector’s defensive components.
Sixthly, Israel Air Force soldiers attacked the area of the Paga Outpost during the raid, but most of the IAF strikes were ineffective due to gaps in coordination with the ground forces.
Lastly, the commanders fell during battle, which affected the decisions that were made and the manner in which the battle was managed. This was exacerbated by the fact that the company commander was unable to reach the command center.
The IDF soldiers who fell defending Paga Outpost included: Capt. Dekel Suissa, St.-Sgt. Tomer Barak, Sgt. Ido Bienenstock, Sgt. Habib Kayan, Sgt. Itamar Cohen, Sgt. Lior Azizov, St-Sgt. Idan Raz, St.-Sgt. Shalev Barnes, St.-Sgt. Itai Glisko, St.-Sgt. Yakir Levi, St.-Sgt. Dolev Amoyal, Sgt. Roi Peri, St.-Sgt. Itamar Ben Yehuda, and St.-Sgt. Chaim Meir Eden.
IDF kills terror cell leader responsible for Paga Outpost attack in Dec. 2024
In December 2024, the IDF and Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) conducted a joint operation to kill Fahmi Salami, commander of Hamas’s Nukhba Brigade in its Zeitoun Battalion.
Salami was the commander of the terror cell that attacked the Paga Outpost.
In 2025, Israeli media reported that approximately 150 terrorists were involved in the attack on the Paga Outpost, with dozens being killed by the IDF on October 7.
What happened at Paga Outpost during the October 7 massacre?
As part of its probe, the IDF published a timeline of events at Paga Outpost on October 7, 2023.
At 5:30 a.m. on October 7, a group from the Golani Brigade's 13th Battalion carried out its "dawn alert" exercise, according to standing orders and the situational assessment known at the time.
Between 5:30 and 6 a.m., the deputy commander of the company positioned at the outpost gave his daily briefing to the forces carrying out operational missions. Armored personnel carrier-based reconnaissance soldiers, an alert response force, and a command post force attended the briefing.
At the conclusion of the briefing, the commander traveled to the IBCT at Sakhaf Valley to check its state of readiness. Additionally, the mortar platoon sergeant briefed the forces positioned in the outpost's mortar compound.
The infiltration and subsequent massacre began at 6:29 a.m.
Phase I: Beginning of the terror attack and activity of the forces in the sector (6:29 a.m. until 6:55 a.m.)
At 6:29 a.m., sirens sounded throughout the sector, and all soldiers present at the outpost, including those from mortar platoons, entered protected areas throughout the outpost. Commanders designated the fortified dining hall as the company assembly point.
At 6:30, the tank commanded by Sakhaf Valley's IBCT commander ordered another tank to move along the perimeter fence toward a specific position. The IBCT commander's tank mobilized to another position along the fence.
At 6:31, the deputy commander of the Paga company ordered the Sakhaf Valley's IBCT to board the Namer Armored Personnel Carriers and tanks. The deputy company commander's command outpost moved from the command post vehicle to a Namer APC. This vehicle remained at the Sakhaf outpost, where the tracker was apparently waiting for the forces to arrive. After several minutes, when the tracker had not arrived at the command post Namer, the soldiers went out to search for him but were unsuccessful.
By 6:32, the deputy commander of the Paga company ordered the IBCT tank commander to move to the same position it had previously occupied, this time with added cover from a Namer APC, and to open fire on any armed individual who crossed a certain point.
At the same time, the mortar platoon's sergeant ordered his soldiers to prepare combat equipment, board the APCs, and prepare the APCs for mortar fire, after receiving reports over the radio that the terror attack was a "complex event."
The platoon sergeant ordered the reconnaissance vehicle force to close the guard post and arrive at the fortified dining hall.
At 6:33 a.m., the alert response force that was stationed near the ANZAC memorial in the Be'eri forest traveled to Paga to take shelter in a protected area. The guard at the rear gate moved to shelter in the concrete cylinder near his position and took shelter in a pillbox after several minutes.
At 6:41 a.m., the deputy commander of the Paga company ordered the IBCT tank commander to open fire at terrorists attempting to cross the fence. Several terrorists were successfully hit in this defensive action.
However, anti-tank missiles were fired at the other tank mobilized to the perimeter fence after it identified four terrorists crossing the fence and received authorization to open fire.
Approximately two minutes later, the IBCT commander's tank was hit by an enemy drone that was launched with a rocket-propelled grenade (RPG) warhead attached to it. As a result, the tank suffered a mechanical malfunction and became stuck in position. The IBCT commander requested an immediate evacuation.
At 6:45 a.m., a tank commanded by St.-Sgt. Shay Levinson closed in on enemy positions and killed 10 terrorists whom Levinson had identified crossing the fence both on foot and in vehicles.
At the same time, the mortar platoon sergeant requested that the battalion command post provide targets to strike with mortar fire.
By 6:49, terrorists had begun firing towards the walls of the outpost from Sakhif Hill.
At 6:50, the IBCT commander's tank reported that the malfunction made it difficult to move and required towing. He also requested the deputy commander of the Paga company to send troops to secure his position.
The deputy battalion commander, who was acting as sector commander at the time, came on the radio at 6:51 a.m. and authorized the mortar platoon to fire shells into the Gaza Strip in response to the terror infiltration. At the same time, a soldier secured in the pillbox position at the Paga Outpost's guard position noticed terrorists firing from Sakhif Hill. The soldier, who did not have radio communications, left the position, ran to the outpost, and entered the dining hall.
Upon arriving at the dining hall, he passed the information to the soldiers stationed there, and in turn it was passed to the outpost commander.
At this stage, soldiers who were in the dining hall were already carrying combat equipment, while others were equipping themselves. The platoon commander issued orders to reinforce the positions and other openings in the outpost.
At 6:52, the deputy company commander updated the outpost commander about terrorists mounted in vehicles who were approaching the outpost and ordered soldiers to reinforce combat positions in order to prevent an infiltration, while maintaining reserve forces for a counterattack on the terrorists. The outpost commander acted accordingly and reinforced defensive positions.
Phase II: Enemy infiltration into the outpost and managing the battles (6:55 a.m. until 8:34 a.m.)
At 6:55 a.m., events worsened as nine terrorists succeeded in infiltrating the outpost through the APC guard post, alongside attacks from terrorist fire coming from Sakhif Hill.
The deputy commander of the Paga company informed the IBCT tank commander that he was unable to come to assist and could only evacuate him after the fighting with the terrorists ended.
By this point, the tank continued to engage and kill infiltrating terrorists until it ran out of ammunition, despite being mechanically disabled from maneuvering.
At 6:56, the other tank, which had charged terrorists near the perimeter fence, was hit by an anti-tank missile. All crew members, except the driver, were seriously wounded.
At this point, the tank stopped, and terrorists abducted the tank's commander. The driver then requested urgent evacuation, and despite not being sure of his exact location, said that he left the "Burma Axis" to move away from the border.
At 6:57 a.m., approximately nine terrorists infiltrated the outpost and split into three squads.
One terror squad attacked the mortar compound from the west, the second opened fire from the northeast, and the third attacked the entrance to the outpost and mortar compound.
Approximately 10 terrorists opened fire and threw grenades at the mortar platoon, which acted quickly to kill four of the terrorists. However, one soldier fell during the encounter, and several others were wounded, including the platoon sergeant.
At the same time, the tank driver reported that he had successfully left the site of the anti-tank missile attack, telling others that the entire crew had been hit, and that he was moving southeast, but found it difficult to orient himself amid the chaos.
After the encounter with the terrorists, the mortar team moved to Paga Outpost through the rear entrance to the gathering point for wounded soldiers, while evacuating the wounded platoon sergeant.
Meanwhile, the battle between the terrorists and mortar platoon continued, during which another two soldiers were murdered. Two other soldiers extricated themselves and took shelter under an APC.
Additionally, two other soldiers fell during this encounter, one at the scene, and another who was seriously wounded and died several months later.
By 7 a.m., the soldiers who had gathered at the company assembly point received orders from the platoon commander, who had taken command of the outpost. The soldiers moved to reinforce positions to defend the outpost.
One squad, under the command of the platoon commander, covered the western side and the entrance to the mortar platoon's position. The second squad, commanded by the platoon sergeant, headed southwest.
Several soldiers were wounded in encounters with terrorists and evacuated to the dining hall.
At 7.01, soldiers requested urgent reinforcements over the company radio. At the same time, a tank was hit by anti-tank fire from the terrorists, who infiltrated the outpost's perimeter from an additional position.
The deputy commander of the Paga company ordered wounded soldiers to be evacuated to the assembly point in the dining hall.
At 7:12, an APC arrived at the outpost. By this stage, the tracker who remained at the Sakhaf outpost was hit by an infiltrating terrorist. They were later declared as having fallen in combat, with their remains taken into the Gaza Strip by terrorists.
At 7:13, soldiers positioned at the outpost engaged terrorists moving on foot towards the northern side of Paga. By this stage, soldiers had formed pairs to provide cover to the bunker entrance, guard post, and southwestern corner of the outpost, respectively.
During a situational assessment, the outpost commander informed the Paga company's deputy commander of an encounter with terrorists, noting that some soldiers were missing certain key combat equipment.
At 7:15, the APC arrived at Paga Outpost, and terrorists who had reached the mortar platoon's compound withdrew northwards on foot. By 7:21, the APC had completed a patrol around the outpost and mortar compound, including locating, firing at, and killing terrorists.
Several calls took place between commanders and soldiers operating at the outpost between 7:34 and 7:56 a.m., during which they communicated reports and updates on the situation on the ground and requested immediate assistance and evacuation of wounded soldiers.
At 7:43, the Israel Air Force sent an aircraft to conduct a disruption strike on the northern side of the outpost, aiming to hold back further attempts at terror infiltration.
At 7:49, soldiers identified a terrorist inside the pillbox at the rear guard post. The Paga company's deputy commander ordered that soldiers fire a shoulder-launched missile towards the terrorist. The outpost commander and two soldiers mobilized to retrieve the missile and moved to a firing position northwest of the outpost; however, terrorists opened fire on them, and one of the soldiers was killed while en route.
At 8:26 a.m., the IBCT commander's tank again requested reinforcements over the radio. The Paga company's deputy commander once again said this would not be possible due to infiltrating terrorists, and said that he would attempt to open protective fire to prevent terrorists from coming closer to the damaged tank, despite the APC also being under attack at the time.
Phase III: Gathering wounded soldiers and continuing the fight against infiltrating terrorists (8:34 a.m. until 10:21 a.m.)
At 8:34, the outpost commander ordered a soldier to bring forces closer to the company assembly point.
By 8:57, the APC had moved to the mortar compound and managed to evacuate two wounded soldiers into the vehicle.
At 9:19, the Paga company's deputy commander discussed with the outpost commander a plan to evacuate wounded soldiers into the dining hall using APCs.
The plan they formulated had two stages. First, two APC drivers would transfer into two APCs parked in the compound. Second, soldiers in the outpost would board the two APCs near the outpost's front guard post.
From 9:23 to 9:27 a.m., the APC commander explained the plan to the outpost commander and emphasized that he would lead the operation and bear overall responsibility. The APC commander also asked the outpost commander to remain available via radio and be prepared to act.
At 9:34 a.m., soldiers positioned at he company assembly point began evacuating wounded soldiers on stretchers towards the dining hall entrance.
A few minutes later, the APC entered the armored vehicle in reverse, near two other parked APCs. During this movement, the soldiers identified a terrorist approaching, who succeeded in attaching an explosive charge to the APC's rear door before fleeing.
The APC's firing slut was malfunctioning, so soldiers were unable to open fire at the terrorist. The charge then exploded, causing a malfunction in the APC's rear entrance door.
Following this incident, a decision was made to evacuate the armored vehicle compound, with the APC moving toward a point south of the outpost.
At 9:41, the APC commander told the outpost commander the plan had failed and that an alternative plan was under consideration. At this stage, soldiers at the outpost returned inside with the wounded to the dining hall, where initial medical treatments were underway.
At 10:11 a.m., the APC left the covering position towards the north. Several minutes later, the APC soldiers spotted and identified approximately 20 terrorists near Sakhif Hill and opened fire at them.
At 10:21, the deputy company commander ordered the APC to move east toward orchards after the heavy machine gun ammunition ran out. The APC moved eastwards and stopped after several hundred meters.
Phase IV: Fighting at the outpost (10:25 a.m. until 4:20 p.m.)
At 10:25 a.m., the outpost commander ordered all soldiers to gather at the company assembly point, understanding that the outpost force was at an operational disadvantage. Terrorists opened fire at soldiers who left the command post on their way to the assembly point.
At 10:27, a combat helicopter arrived in the sector and opened fire to disrupt terrorist activity.
At approximately 10:35, the outpost commander and his partner provided cover for soldiers moving toward the assembly point. They encountered several terrorists at the guard post.
During this encounter, the outpost commander was wounded in his hand, but continued to close in on terrorist infiltrators. The two soldiers killed several terrorists during the encounter before falling in combat later.
At 11 a.m., terrorists attempted to infiltrate the outpost via the mortar platoon's entrance. Soldiers manning a covering position withdrew towards the western pillbox.
Between 11:30 and 11:35 a.m., an IAF unmanned aerial vehicle attacked near the dining hall and other parts of the outpost, killing several terrorists. This successfully disrupted the terrorists' attack on the company assembly point.
At 11:45, another exchange of fire took place, during which at least one terrorist was killed. At this time, six soldiers formed a unified force under the command of the platoon sergeant, who spoke with the company commander. The commander, at Sa'ad Junction at the time, updated the sergeant on the operational situation and said the force was under heavy fire from all directions.
In light of the situation, the platoon sergeant decided to break contact with the outpost.
At 11:50, the unified force began moving in a secured formation through the exit opening in the wall toward the front guard post. During its movement, the force identified and killed a terrorist. Afterward, the company commander instructed the sergeant to link up with the APC outside the outpost.
From noon until 12:15 p.m., the sergeant's force linked up with the APC commander. At the same time, soldiers in the dining hall dragged tables and other equipment to block openings and engaged in prolonged fighting with terrorists who attempted to infiltrate, including by throwing grenades and shooting at soldiers.
At 1 p.m., terrorists set fire to both sides of the dining hall. Soldiers inside began to suffer from smoke inhalation, suffocation, and clouded consciousness as a result.
At 1:10 p.m., a soldier exited the western opening of the dining hall and killed two terrorists.
By 1:13, five soldiers decided to leave the dining hall and fight terrorists outside. Two of the soldiers went toward the kitchen while three went toward the lounge area of the outpost. All five fell in close combat against a large number of terrorists who were positioned at the dining hall exits.
At 1:19 p.m., a combat helicopter opened fire at the terrorists' pickup truck, which was moving through the outpost, but was unable to hit it. The pickup truck broke out of the outpost and fled.
Phase V: Arrival of rescue forces and reinforcements (4:20 p.m. until the evening of October 7)
At 4:20 p.m., a rescue force, including counterterrorism soldiers from the IDF's "Lotar" unit and officers from the Golani Brigade, arrived at the outpost.
These reinforcements cleared the outpost, linked up with soldiers within, and evacuated both the wounded and the fallen.
No terrorists remained in the compound when the rescue forces arrived.
The rescue force returned for a second time to collect the remains of the fallen during the evening, at which time a soldier was killed by an anti-tank missile that hit the rescue vehicle.

Boy George stands with Israel, so where are the rest of the world's artists? - editorial
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
03:12:31 UTC
12:12:31 KST

Nine years ago this week, Chrissie Hynde, the leader of the world-famous rock band The Pretenders, took to the stage at Tel Aviv’s Menorah Mivtahim Arena, waving a giant Israeli flag, as the appreciative crowd in the sold-out venue roared its approval.
Imagine a similar scene taking place today, because that’s what one would have to do, as the actuality of it happening – with Hynde or with anyone else of her stature – is virtually unfathomable in the post-October 7 massacre demonization of Israel that has taken place globally.
Israel has virtually – at best – been shunned by the international artistic community; at worst, exercised by the Mark Ruffalos and Javier Bardems of the world, it has become the stomping ground for accusations and half-truths bordering on rabid antisemitism.
More nuanced, and perhaps even more worrisome, is the black hole that British pop superstar Ed Sheeran fell into for trying to diffuse the whole Macklemore “Free Palestine” cancellation scandal that made headlines worldwide.
Sheeran attempted to express understanding and empathy for both sides in the conflict, saying: “What happened in Israel and at the Nova music festival on October 7th was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain.”
Even though he then implied that Israel was responsible for the “catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate” situation in Gaza, Sheeran was vilified by the pro-Palestinian community.
That’s why when an artist shows full frontal support for Israel – in words and actions – it’s vital to point it out. American comedian and actor Michael Rappaport and British 1980s pop singer Boy George have unabashedly stood by Israel since the October 7 massacre. Rappaport has visited and performed in the country numerous times, and he’ll be returning next week to headline the biannual Comedy for Koby comedy series throughout the country.
The non-Jewish George this year released a song – “We Will Dance Again” – in which he eulogized the victims of the Supernova music festival, criticized those who claim Israel has committed genocide in Gaza, and declared: “I stand with the Jews.” On Tuesday, he announced that he’ll be coming to Israel in November to perform in Tel Aviv.
Rappaport, George, along with a paltry few others, have bucked the trend and put their consciences ahead of their careers by not hiding their heads in the sand. Which raised the disturbing question: Why haven’t more artists – Jewish and gentile – done the same?
Where are Bob Dylan, Paul Simon?
Where has Bob Dylan been the last three years, or Paul Simon, two of the most influential Jewish artists of the 20th century? They know very well that Israel doesn’t deliberately kill Palestinian children or commit genocide. They easily could have showed up with an acoustic guitar and given a morale boost to the country, much like Leonard Cohen did during the Yom Kippur War in 1973.
On the contrary, Simon’s only public expression since October 7, 2023, was to sign a petition calling for the release from prison of Marwan Barghouti, who is serving multiple life sentences for the murders of Israelis. Dylan has been silent.
Likewise, why hasn’t Madonna – who has visited Israel numerous times – made a quick visit to Tel Aviv and shown the world that even if Israel may have made mistakes over the last three years, it still is a country that doesn’t deserve to be demonized for defending itself?
Why hasn’t U2 frontman Bono – who so eloquently eulogized the victims of the Supernova music festival from a US stage and who has appeared in Israel – made a symbolic visit?
Easier to stay silent than to address Israeli-Palestinian conflict
Sometimes, as Ed Sheeran learned, it’s easier to say nothing than to wade into the minefields of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict – which makes those who do jump in and stand with good vs evil all the more admirable.
In November, when he performs at the same arena that Hynde did nine years ago, George will undoubtedly reenact the flag-waving scene, and the crowd will once again shake the rafters in pride.
He deserves all the credit in the world for his willingness to ride against the tide by standing with Israel – not only in spirit, but with his glittery shoes on the ground in Tel Aviv.
But it raises the glaring question: Where is everyone else? The answer, it seems, is blowing in the morally subjective wind.

Nearly two-thirds of Americans believe the United States is not winning the war with Iran, while approval of US President Donald Trump's handling of foreign affairs has fallen to a new low, according to a CNN poll conducted by SSRS and released Tuesday.
The poll found that 64% of Americans said the US was not winning the war, compared with 36% who believed it was.
Trump's handling of the conflict received approval from 26% of respondents. His broader handling of foreign affairs received 29% approval and 71% disapproval, the lowest foreign policy approval rating recorded for Trump in a CNN poll across either of his presidential terms.
The decline was particularly pronounced among Republicans.
Sixty percent of Republicans approved of Trump's handling of the situation in Iran, down 13 percentage points from 73% in March, according to the poll.
Republican support for Trump's handling of Iran drops
CNN reported that Democrats and independents had already registered lower levels of approval, meaning the more recent decline was driven largely by changing views among Republicans.
The poll was released as Trump attended the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where Iran and the ongoing war featured prominently in his foreign policy agenda.
Trump addressed the General Assembly on Tuesday, saying Iran must not be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon and raising the prospect of either reaching an agreement with Tehran or further military action.
US, Iran hold indirect contacts at UNGA
The polling comes as Washington and Tehran have resumed indirect contact after months without talks.
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner communicated with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi through mediators on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on Wednesday, The Jerusalem Post reported.
The contacts were the first between the two sides since an interim ceasefire agreement collapsed in July.
Trump described the meeting between US officials and Iran's mediators as "very productive" and said he believed there was momentum toward an agreement.
Iran, meanwhile, communicated conditions through Qatar that included an end to the war on all fronts and an end to what Tehran described as US "acts of aggression."

Jewish teacher in Philadelphia pretended to be Palestinian for years
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
03:11:30 UTC
12:11:30 KST

A Jewish public school teacher and pro-Palestinian advocate in Philadelphia has admitted to fabricating Palestinian, Tunisian, and Black heritage to her colleagues for years, in a case that some online commenters are dubbing “the Palestinian Rachel Dolezal.”
Hannah Gann posted confessions and apologies to social media this week, following confrontations from local pro-Palestinian groups she had worked with. In her apologies, she identified herself as “a white woman with significant privilege and wealth” who has “no Palestinian or Tunisian heritage.”
A Jewish Telegraphic Agency request for comment to Gann was not immediately returned.
Two local activist groups Gann had been involved with, Philly Educators for Palestine and Racial Justice Organizing Committee, said in their own statement that Gann was also “of Jewish heritage and [part of] an Israeli settler family.” They further accused Gann of falsely claiming to be Black at various points, until they confronted her about her background days ago.
Comparisons to Dolezal, a white woman who posed as Black for years, taught Africana college courses and held a leadership role with a local NAACP branch before being exposed in 2015, spread over the Internet on Wednesday.
Gann says she 'outright lied' to everyone about her background
“I hid the truth or outright lied about my background to everyone in my life,” Gann, a teacher at West Philadelphia’s The Workshop School, said in her own Instagram video message on Monday. “I hid my family’s background from everyone in Philly and also hid from the people in my own family what I was doing.”
Neither of Gann’s visible social media apologies mentioned Jewish heritage. But the Philadelphia Inquirer, citing internal documents from the activist groups, reported that she had identified herself in college as a “Jewish woman with family in the occupied West Bank.”
Gann had also told colleagues her grandfather was born in Palestine, when he was reportedly born in Baltimore, according to documents cited by the Inquirer. Fellow activists accused her of having darkened her skin using makeup and fake tan and adopting a Black American accent after returning from a stint in the Peace Corps in Rwanda.
As with Dolezal, commenters accused Gann of posing as a member of a marginalized group of color to gain clout.
“When marginalization becomes a form of social currency some people will always do this,” one account under the name “regretmaxxing” wrote in Gann’s comments.
Gann had made the pro-Palestinian cause central to her identity over the years, including a teach-in at her school in 2024 to protest “scholasticide” in Gaza, the Inquirer reported. That year she also told a local media outlet that the right-wing group Accuracy in Media had displayed her name on a truck calling her “Philadelphia’s Leading Antisemite.”
Accuracy in Media, which has targeted activists in other states using similar methods, confirmed to JTA that they had also done so to Gann.
Gann remains a firm supporter of Palestinians
“Hannah Gann remains one of Philadelphia’s leading antisemites,” the group’s founder, Adam Guillette, said in a statement, linking to a video of his group’s truck displaying the message outside the school where Gann worked.
Delivering testimony to the Philadelphia Board of Education in December 2025, Gann, wearing a keffiyeh, urged them to “treat Islamophobia, anti-Black and anti-Palestinian racism just as seriously as you treat allegations of antisemitism.”
“Why are Jewish staff members’ experiences immediately assumed to indicate systemic failures, while Black, brown and Muslim students’ testimonies are treated as isolated incidents?” she continued, shortly before a board member cut off her mic.
A fellow teacher of Gann’s said on Instagram that Gann had told her, following a trip to Israel in 2023, that she had both Jewish and Palestinian people in her family, later claiming that her grandfather had been an anti-Zionist Jew born in Mandatory Palestine who left over disagreements with the direction of Israel.
“We will no longer work with Hannah, and she will no longer be welcome in any of our organizing spaces,” the pro-Palestinian groups said in their own statement.
A biography of Gann still visible on the West Philly Participatory Defense Hub, a different local organizing group, describes her as having “loved ones directly impacted by the criminal (in)justice system” and notes that she is a member of The First Unitarian Church.
In her apology, which she posted on Yom Kippur, Gann argued that her advocacy was genuine even though her persona was not.
“The fact that I lied about who I was does not mean anyone else who speaks up for Palestine is lying and does not erase the urgency of listening to voices on the ground,” she said. She added that she would be “deleting anything posted by Zionists.”

Live: Netanyahu faces UN over Gaza as Abbas set to address assembly by video

AI could harm children more than social media – ex-Google exec
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
03:10:55 UTC
12:10:55 KST

AI could harm children more than social media – ex-Google exec
Artificial intelligence could pose greater risks to children than social media, with tech companies failing to put adequate safeguards in place, a former Google safety executive has warned.
Tom Siegel, who founded Google’s trust and safety team and spent 15 years at the company, told Reuters this week that the industry was repeating mistakes made during the rise of social media.
“We find ourselves in a really terrible situation in terms of what AI is doing to kids,” Siegel said. “The idea that the industry will figure it out by itself without outside help is unrealistic.”
He warned of “very severe scenarios of harm,” citing risks ranging from suicide and psychosis to ‘cognitive offloading’ – reduced critical thinking caused by relying on AI for answers. Companies can and should take immediate steps, including stronger age checks to prevent children from accessing chatbots, he said.
Google has insisted that its AI search features help young users learn and explore information, telling Reuters that parents can block a child’s access to its search engine entirely. However, an internal Meta policy document, exposed by the publication last year, allowed its chatbots to engage children in conversations that could be “romantic or sensual,” prompting a congressional investigation.
Major social media platforms have faced years of lawsuits over claims of harm to children and teenagers. Meta recently agreed to a $17 billion settlement with California and 28 other US states over accusations that Facebook and Instagram were deliberately designed to keep minors hooked, while denying wrongdoing. Thousands of similar cases have been filed in the US.
Governments have also moved to restrict children’s access to social media. Australia last year became the first country to require major platforms to prevent under-16s from holding accounts. About 4.7 million minors’ accounts were restricted shortly after the rules took effect.
The EU last week proposed barring children under 13 from social media and allowing those aged 13 and 14 to use only restricted accounts managed by a parent or guardian. The proposed rules would also cover AI companions and chatbots.
Siegel’s warning comes as prominent tech executives, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI chief Sam Altman, xAI chief Elon Musk and Google DeepMind co-founder Demis Hassabis, have backed calls to slow the development of increasingly powerful AI systems. Anthropic researcher Evan Hubinger this month said he personally believes there is a greater than 10% chance that AI could “kill all humans” within the next decade.

Expert urges prioritizing protection of children from haze in Southeast Asia
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
10:59:57 CST
11:59:57 KST

KUALA LUMPUR, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- The ongoing haze in Southeast Asia has pushed air quality to hazardous levels, with children especially vulnerable to heightened physiological and developmental risks from airborne pollution, according to an expert.
Children are particularly vulnerable because their lungs and immune systems are still developing. They also inhale more air relative to their body weight, with physical exertion further increasing their exposure to PM2.5, fine particulate matter that can penetrate deep into the lungs, Sapna Shridhar Patil, Senior Lecturer in Public Health at Taylor's University, told Xinhua.
"Haze can disrupt health and learning. Haze may cause coughing, nasal congestion, headaches, fatigue and breathing difficulties. Even relatively mild symptoms can affect a student's concentration, classroom participation and attendance," she said.
Beyond physical ailments, missing sports and social activities, spending prolonged periods indoors and worrying about worsening symptoms may also affect children's emotional wellbeing, Sapna said.
Malaysia and other countries in the region have seen poor air quality in recent weeks due to prolonged hot and dry weather and haze resulting from numerous fires. ■

Interview: Pinglu Canal to deepen Malaysia-China logistics, industrial cooperation: Malaysian business leader
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
10:59:34 CST
11:59:34 KST

KUALA LUMPUR, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- The opening of China's Pinglu Canal will significantly shorten transport distances and reduce logistics costs between ASEAN and western China, while creating new opportunities for Malaysian enterprises to expand their presence in the Chinese market, a Malaysian business leader has said.
Looi Hei Tyng, deputy president of The Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia (ACCCIM), told Xinhua in a recent interview that the canal will not only enhance regional connectivity but also encourage enterprises to expand their cooperation beyond traditional trade into industrial and supply chain activities.
The 134.2-kilometer canal, stretching from Hengzhou in Guangxi to the Beibu Gulf, opened on Sept. 16. It is the closest maritime outlet for much of southwest China.
Looi noted that the opening of the Pinglu Canal will mark not only the completion of a major infrastructure project but also an important step towards building a more integrated logistics network in western China.
By linking inland waterways with maritime routes, the canal will further improve China's transport network, he added.
Looking ahead, Looi called for better connections between the canal and existing port, rail and road networks to facilitate multimodal transport.
In addition to selling products to western China, Malaysian enterprises could engage in warehousing and distribution, processing and manufacturing, supply chain management, and cross-border e-commerce in Guangxi and other parts of western China, he said.
Such cooperation would help strengthen two-way investment ties between Malaysia and China, he added.
China and ASEAN have been each other's largest trading partner for years. Bilateral trade surpassed 1 trillion U.S. dollars for the first time in 2025, reaching 1.05 trillion dollars. In the first eight months of 2026, bilateral trade totaled 862.75 billion dollars, up 25.6 percent year on year. ■

China remains world's largest industrial robot market: report
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
10:59:18 CST
11:59:18 KST

BERLIN, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- China accounted for nearly three-fifths of industrial robots installed worldwide in 2025, further strengthening its position as the world's largest market for industrial robotics, according to the World Robotics 2026 report released Thursday.
A total of 354,000 industrial robots were deployed in China last year, up 20 percent from 2024 and accounting for 59 percent of global installations, said the Frankfurt-based International Federation of Robotics (IFR) in the report. The figure was nearly 60,000 units higher than the previous annual record.
"The success of China in modernizing its industrial system is based on its national robotics strategy, which was initiated ten years ago," said IFR President Jane Heffner.
She added that an updated strategy under China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) aims to focus artificial intelligence (AI) research on physical applications, with robots serving as an important driver of economic growth.
China's demand for industrial robots was led by the electrical and electronics, automotive, and metal and machinery industries. The electrical and electronics industry installed 96,400 industrial robots in 2025, up 16 percent year on year and accounting for 27 percent of China's total installations. The automotive industry installed 78,900 units, up 38 percent and reaching a record high, while installations in the metal and machinery industry rose 44 percent to 78,700 units.
Chinese robot makers also continued to expand their presence in the domestic market. Installations by domestic suppliers rose 15 percent in 2025 to 195,000 units, giving them a 55-percent share of total installations. Installations by foreign suppliers increased 27 percent. More than half of the industrial robots installed in China have been supplied by Chinese brands since 2024, the IFR said.
The IFR forecasts that the Chinese market for industrial robots is far from saturated, with annual growth of 5 to 10 percent on average likely through 2029. Demographic changes and resulting labor shortages are expected to continue driving demand for robotic automation, which can help make production more resilient to labor shortages, it said.
Guided by the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), China's robotics strategy emphasizes technological self-reliance and the modernization of traditional industries, the IFR said. It added that China's robotics industry is moving toward becoming an innovator in physical AI and a developer of intelligent industrial robotics. ■
